[179] A defense for our time Recommendation from the Ministry of Defense on March 23, 2012, approved by the Cabinet the same day

[180] Stoltenberg II Government

[181] Introduction – status and main priorities 1.1 The role and function of the Armed Forces

[182] Norway must at all times have the relevant means of force at its disposal to counter pressure, aggression or attacks

[183] With modern capabilities and high responsiveness, the Armed Forces will constitute a war-preventing threshold that entails high risk and cost for anyone who might challenge Norwegian security and independence

[184] Norway has been spared from military aggression against its own territory for more than two generations

[185] This is not least due to the fact that we are linked to a collective security organization through NATO membership

[186] At the same time, Norway has maintained a defense system adapted to the security policy challenges of changing eras

[187] Although the basic functions of the Armed Forces remain fixed over time, each generation must develop and adapt the Armed Forces to the needs of the times

[188] Based on the successful restructuring of the Armed Forces since 2001, the government will present the basis for further developing a relevant defense that ensures Norwegian security with this long-term plan

[189] NATO remains the cornerstone of Norwegian security policy

[190] Serious threats or attacks against Norwegian or allied security must be handled within the framework of NATO's collective defense

[191] NATO constitutes the most important conflict prevention threshold in our immediate vicinity

[192] The combined capabilities of the armed forces are an important contribution to the alliance's war-preventing function

[193] The most important rationale of the Armed Forces is to defend Norway and Norwegian interests and values ​​against external threats and attacks

[194] However, in today's globalized world, safety and security must be considered in a broad context

[195] It is in Norway's interest to contribute to international peace and stability by participating in efforts to maintain a UN-led international legal order, defend human rights and strengthen intergovernmental cooperation

[196] The Norwegian Armed Forces constitute a significant element in Norway's international efforts in these areas

[197] In recent years, the Armed Forces have contributed to a number of demanding operations outside Norway's borders

[198] It has demonstrated Norway's ability and willingness to uphold our commitments, show international solidarity and contribute to burden sharing

[199] The defense is primarily designed to handle external aggression or pressure against Norway, primarily in relation to other states

[200] At the same time, Prop

[201] A defense for our time

[202] The Norwegian Armed Forces have many capabilities that can make important contributions in other crisis situations

[203] All of society's resources must be able to be deployed in a joint effort if our society is put to a serious test

[204] Smooth and rational cross-sectoral collaboration requires a clear division of responsibilities and well-established arrangements and procedures for the collaboration

[205] At the same time, it is important that everything is done to ensure that resources can be utilized quickly and with the best possible effect in meeting current needs

[206] This requires, among other things, good knowledge in other sectors about what the Armed Forces can contribute in various crisis situations, and regular exercises to build mutual experience and expertise

[207] A new planning process In the St.prop

[208] No. 48 (2007–

[209] – A defense to protect Norway's security, interests and values – the government announced that development of the defense sector will take place through more continuous strategic and long-term development work within the framework of the integrated Ministry of Defense

[210] The changed planning model does not change the practice of presenting overall long-term plans to the Storting

[211] Long-term plans with broad support in the Storting are an important tool for ensuring long-term sustainability and consensus on defense policy

[212] Such plans will therefore continue to be a foundation for the development of the defense sector

[213] The Government will therefore aim to ensure that the Storting, during each parliamentary term, has the opportunity to consider an overall perspective on developments in the defence sector

[214] At the same time, the restructuring involves several important changes

[215] The defense sector's long-term planning is no longer unilaterally centered around fixed, four-year planning periods

[216] The long-term plans will no longer be comprehensive reassessments in which the entire structure of the Armed Forces is drawn up from scratch

[217] The plans will be to a greater extent describe the ongoing work to develop the sector

[218] This long-term plan builds on the robust foundation established with Parliamentary Proposal No. 48 (2007–

[219] The plan is therefore somewhat more selective than previous plans

[220] Where there is a need to inform about adjustments or make new decisions, a broad presentation is provided with justifications and descriptions of consequences as a basis for the Storting's consideration

[221] In areas where the Storting's consideration of St. prp

[222] No. 48 (2007–2008) is still valid and the main course is unchanged, the presentation is somewhat more general

[223] It also means that the space devoted to certain topics should not be perceived as a signal of emphasis or prioritization

[224] When the Air Force is given significantly more space in this proposition than the Navy, it is because, for example, the Air Force is to implement a number of reforms, particularly related to the modernization of the combat air force, while the changes for the Navy are smaller

[225] Cross-prioritization based on a balanced and holistic perspective remains crucial for the further development of the defense sector, in terms of renewal and improvement of organization and operational structure, as well as financial and administrative conditions

[226] The Ministry of Defence continuously studies the development of the defence sector and handles challenges as needs arise

[227] When such processes make it desirable or necessary to inform the Storting, this will be done in an appropriate manner

[228] The primary purpose of the long-term plans will be to provide a holistic perspective and present issues that are ripe for decision

[229] A long-term perspective

[230] The Armed Forces have undergone a long and intensive period of restructuring

[231] it was emphasized that the restructuring had entered a new phase with an emphasis on continuous development and adaptation to changes in needs and framework conditions

[232] This perspective is still valid

[233] However, the modernization of the Armed Forces is a process that will never be complete

[234] Today's challenges require a continuously updated, flexible and mobile emergency defense force that can quickly meet various challenges at home and abroad

[235] Such a defense cannot be built up overnight

[236] The expertise is specialized and requires a long time to develop

[237] The material and technology have long lead times

[238] In areas where a defense organization fails to keep up with developments, it is very challenging to catch up

[239] The requirement for short-notice efforts therefore requires continuous and long-term planning

[240] In defense policy, Norway has a heavy responsibility towards the rising generation

[241] Decisions today create the Armed Forces of tomorrow

[242] Neglect today can create future gaps

[243] The government places great emphasis on establishing a long-term, 2011–2012 Prop

[244] A defense for our time: a comprehensive and forward-looking perspective on the development of the Armed Forces

[245] Therefore, this long-term plan describes a defense structure in continuous development and renewal

[246] The fundamental purpose of this renewal is to continue the Armed Forces' general level of ambition – a pause in the renewal processes would have meant that the Armed Forces' operational capabilities would have quickly become obsolete and degraded

[247] At the same time, it must be emphasized that the measures and investments that have been undertaken in recent years, together with the investments described in this plan, will in many areas increase the Armed Forces' ability to carry out its tasks

[248] The acquisition of new combat aircraft and the adaptation of the army structure, together with the significant renewal of the Navy's vessels in recent years, will overall provide a significantly improved operational capability

[249] Efficiency measures and improved management of the defense sector further contribute to freeing up resources that strengthen the Armed Forces' effectiveness

[250] With this long-term plan, the government presents a defense structure that both consolidates and further develops the ability to secure Norway's interests and values

[255] The financial framework established for 2009–2012 involved a focus on the defense sector in terms of appropriations

[256] The long-term plan for these years envisaged a gradual escalation of the defence budget from the 2008 level of NOK 31.54 billion to a level that is NOK 800 million higher, measured in 2008 kroner

[257] The government has followed up on the increase in appropriations in the defense budget that the current long-term plan envisaged

[258] At the same time, significant additional amounts have been allocated for international operations in the period 2009–2012, including Afghanistan and Libya

[259] The real level of appropriations during the period is therefore higher than the budget increase of NOK 800 million indicates

[260] Another basic prerequisite for the St.prp

[261] No. 48 (2007–2008) was to reallocate funds from lower to higher priority activities

[262] At the same time as the increase in appropriations, the defense sector has therefore implemented significant internal efficiency improvements and organizational changes

[263] The resource-freeing measures are comprehensive and cover, among other things, the dismantling of bases and other infrastructure and the streamlining of internal processes in the defense sector

[264] At the same time, the level of material investment has been lower compared to the level in the previous long-term plan

[265] Together with the increase in appropriations, the resource-freeing measures will create a more lasting balance between the Armed Forces' tasks, structure and resources

[266] Furthermore, some important decisions have been made that result in a higher operating level than was initially planned

[267] Priority initiatives such as strengthening the Intelligence Service, strengthening the National Security Authority, environmental remediation of contaminated seabeds, expanded operation-specific joint training before deployment abroad, and care for veterans are examples of such decisions

[268] The Armed Forces have consistently modernized departments and acquired new capabilities that lead to improved responsiveness, endurance and quality, which in turn contributes to the ability to carry out assigned tasks being significantly strengthened

[313] Dimensioning, adapting and further developing the Armed Forces' expertise and personnel structure are crucial to achieving the goals of improved ability to solve tasks and establishing a more lasting balance between the Armed Forces' tasks, structure and resources

[314] In recent years, the Armed Forces have placed emphasis on adapting the personnel structure to the needs of the operational defence, including by adjusting the composition of the various personnel categories and the rank structure

[315] Man-years have been redistributed from lower to higher priority areas, and staffing in the Armed Forces is being shifted towards priority areas

[316] This contributes to strengthening the Armed Forces' operational capability in accordance with the goals of the long-term plan, ensures better endurance in operations nationally and abroad, reduces attrition in certain categories of key personnel, and improves personnel coverage within selected areas

[317] Adapting the personnel structure is a continuous process

[319] The main themes in this long-term plan are

[320] Competence and personnel

[321] The defense sector's ability to attract, develop and manage expertise will be a key challenge in the years to come

[322] The long-term plan describes the overall challenge picture that is the starting point for a major study that will ensure that the management of personnel and expertise meets the needs of a modern operational defense

[323] Improvement, management and governance

[324] Continuous improvement, development and adaptation within the overall financial framework are a prerequisite for continuing the modernization of the Armed Forces

[325] Strengthened ability to manage and implement improvement measures contributes to sustainable and balanced development of the structure

[337] The Government's main priorities

[338] In implementing this long-term plan, the Government will give particular priority to

[339] – Strengthen the Armed Forces' ability to constitute a war-preventing threshold by further developing

[340] The Armed Forces' overall capabilities and consider military capabilities in a holistic perspective, both nationally and in an allied context. – Contribute to international operations to ensure international peace and stability, promote a UN-led world order and contribute to NATO's overall stabilizing and war-preventing capability and effectiveness

[341] – Further develop the defense sector's ability to assist civil society in crisis situations in a flexible and effective manner, by facilitating regular exercises with other sectors and agencies, including clarifying roles and responsibilities

[342] – Strengthen work on preventive security and ICT security across social sectors

[343] – Address the defense sector's competence challenges through a competence reform that will further develop the sector's ability to attract, recruit, develop and employ the right personnel with the right competence, while at the same time safeguarding employees

[344] These priorities are specified in chapter

[345] A defense for our time

[346] Frames and guides

[347] The Armed Forces shall, alone and together with allies, safeguard Norwegian sovereignty, Norwegian rights, interests and values

[348] Through its ability to provide an adapted and relevant response across the entire spectrum of conflicts, the Norwegian Defence Forces shall constitute a war-preventing threshold that ensures Norway's security and freedom of action against political, military and other forms of pressure

[349] In today's world, security must be considered in a global perspective

[350] Norway cannot therefore limit its security policy outlook to its own immediate areas

[351] It is in Norway's interest to contribute to international peace and stability by participating in efforts to maintain a UN-led international legal order, defend human rights and strengthen intergovernmental cooperation

[352] The armed forces are one of the instruments in Norway's contribution to creating a safer world

[353] Although the Norwegian Armed Forces' most important role is to defend Norway against external threats and attacks, the Norwegian Armed Forces' capabilities can also make valuable contributions in other crisis situations

[354] The Armed Forces possess unique resources and expertise that can supplement civilian authorities' crisis management when needed

[355] The Armed Forces have undergone a long and demanding period of restructuring

[356] Although the major restructuring has now been completed, the Armed Forces must be continuously developed to meet current needs

[357] With this long-term plan, the government presents measures that ensure that the Armed Forces continue to be a relevant instrument for securing Norwegian interests and values

[374] Security policy framework and developments

[375] Norway has the following main security policy objectives: – To prevent war and the emergence of various threats to Norwegian and collective security. – To contribute to peace, stability and the further development of a UN-led international legal order. – To safeguard Norwegian sovereignty, Norwegian rights, interests and values and protect Norwegian freedom of action against political, military and other pressure

[376] – Together with our allies, defend Norway and NATO against attacks and threats. – To secure society against attacks and threats from state and non-state actors

[377] A strong and well-functioning UN is a prerequisite for the development of a multilateral world order based on international law and human rights

[378] In Norwegian security policy, NATO is the cornerstone within the overall framework of the UN

[379] The Alliance is now focusing more attention on its own region, and will wind down the ISAF operation in Afghanistan by

[380] A major challenge for NATO is the reductions in member states' defense spending. 2011–

[381] A defense for our time response appropriations as a result of the economic crisis

[382] The dynamic developments in the Asia-Pacific region, especially China, are causing the United States to focus more attention on this region

[383] This means that Europe receives less attention

[384] In the future, European countries must expect to take on a greater share of the alliance's burden in collective defense

[385] For NATO and Norway, it is crucial to safeguard the transatlantic security community and to ensure stability and security

[386] It is important for Norway to safeguard its own interests in its neighbouring areas, especially in the high north

[387] This means maintaining NATO's presence and continuing cooperation with Russia and the other neighbors in the High North and the Arctic

[388] For Norway, it is of particular interest to contribute to good cooperation between Russia and the Western security community

[389] This is important both for international development in general and for stability in our immediate areas in particular

[390] The combination of Russian great power ambitions, interests in the High North and military buildup means that stability in the North may be challenged in the future

[391] To contribute to predictability and stability, Norway will continue to maintain a high level of military presence in the North

[392] A number of broad international trends contribute to uncertainty about the security policy challenges Norway will face in the future

[393] Among these are the continued globalization, the rise of new great powers and the shift in economic power

[394] The relationship between the United States and China will have great significance for the international security policy climate

[395] China is today the world's second largest economy and the world's largest exporting nation

[396] The United States remains a leader in terms of global political and military influence

[397] However, China's economic growth lays the foundation for a comprehensive modernization of the country's forces

[398] The proliferation of weapons of mass destruction is a persistent threat to international security and stability

[399] Iran and North Korea in particular have long been a cause for concern

[400] Several countries that may be on the verge of acquiring nuclear weapons have also made significant progress in developing long-range missiles

[401] This is an important background for NATO's development of missile defense

[402] Terrorism is a continuous threat that has gained global prevalence

[403] International terrorism originating in militant Islamist circles remains the most prominent threat, but we are increasingly seeing that other ideological currents can also be the source of terrorist acts

[404] Attacks in the digital space are one of the threats that have grown the most in recent years

[405] The threat goes hand in hand with a constant expansion in the use of digital technology in practically all sectors of society, making advanced societies like our own increasingly vulnerable to digital attacks

[406] Advanced state and non-state actors are conducting extensive digital operations, including to gain access to sensitive information in other countries

[407] Such operations mean that greater emphasis must be placed on defensive measures

[408] The Armed Forces will strengthen the ability for preventive security in the digital space and contribute to strengthening national and allied defense capabilities in the field

[409] In this environment, Norway will give special priority to four areas within security and defense policy

[410] Firstly, it is crucial to contribute to NATO's relevance and credibility through force contributions and contributions to the development of NATO's defence against new threats

[411] Key priorities will also be stronger ties between allied and Norwegian command structures, and facilitation of allied advance operations

[412] Secondly, Norway will prioritize national measures, especially by maintaining a high level of ambition for the maintenance of the Armed Forces' national tasks and presence in its own local areas

[413] Thirdly, Norway will facilitate expanded multinational defense cooperation to reduce costs and maintain the alliance's overall military capacity for collective defense

[414] Fourth, we will continue to prioritize contributions to international crisis management across the full spectrum of peace operations

[415] Norway places great emphasis on the use of military force being anchored in the UN Charter and that all relevant parts of the defence structure should be able to contribute, so that both burdens and acquired expertise are distributed within the organisation

[416] Societal developments

[417] The armed forces are an integrated part of society and interact with their surroundings

[418] Planning for the future development of the Armed Forces must therefore take into account a broad spectrum of developments, including those outside the security policy area

[419] Society has become more vulnerable, partly as a result of increased centralization, specialization and dependence on technology

[420] The ability to contribute to societal security has therefore become more important

[421] At the same time, the Armed Forces have become more dependent on civil society when it comes to providing expertise and delivering goods, services and technology

[422] The ability to cooperate flexibly with civil society has consequently become increasingly central to Forsvaret

[423] A defense for our time

[424] This applies both in a normal situation, during various crises or in war

[425] Also in multinational operations outside Norway's borders, there are increased demands on cooperation and coordination with civilian actors

[426] It requires flexibility combined with clarity around roles and responsibilities

[427] Society is characterized by an ever-increasing diversity: ethnic, cultural, linguistic, knowledge-based and experiential

[428] The Armed Forces aim to reflect society's diversity to a greater extent

[429] This is important both because it will improve the Armed Forces' ability to handle complex challenges and because it will strengthen the Armed Forces' legitimacy and support among the population

[430] The economic turmoil following the 2008 financial crisis is affecting the defense sector in many countries

[431] Most of our NATO allies and partners are reducing their defense budgets

[432] Several countries have been forced to make extensive cuts in the defense sector

[433] Norway, on the other hand, has experienced renewed economic growth since the summer of 2009 and employment has picked up

[434] Long-term and sufficiently tight governance, combined with good management of petroleum revenues, has contributed to Norway having a unique economic freedom of action

[435] This has provided room to strengthen defense budgets

[436] In addition, Norway has worked for several years to modernize the Armed Forces and at the same time establish a good and sustainable balance between resources, tasks, level of ambition and operational capability

[437] The restructuring of the Armed Forces since 2001 has been based on clear choices and priorities to ensure good integrity

[438] Compared with many of our allies and partners, Norway therefore has the best conditions for further developing a defense with modern and future-oriented capabilities

[439] At the same time, the difficult global economic situation also creates challenges for Norway and for Norwegian defense and security policy

[440] Norway is closely intertwined in the globalized world economy and is influenced by international economic trends

[441] In a security policy sense, Norway is also part of a collective community through NATO

[442] If our partners are forced to reduce their defenses, it could ultimately affect the alliance's ability to fulfill its tasks

[443] Multinational cooperation and integration in the field of defense has received increasing attention in recent years

[444] This is not only because many countries are experiencing pressure on their defense budgets due to the economic situation, but is also related to cost developments in military technology

[445] Many countries are therefore seeking increased cooperation in the development, acquisition, operation and maintenance of defense equipment, as well as closer cooperation within the framework of international operations

[446] It is in Norway's interest to increase its participation in such cooperation

[447] The government's goal is for Norway to be a pioneer in sustainable development in the environmental field

[448] The defense sector takes responsibility for its part of the national environmental policy and must apply an environmentally conscious perspective to all activities

[449] Defence policy framework and guidelines

[450] Defense policy objectives arise from security policy objectives

[451] Within its area of responsibility and in cooperation with other national authorities where this is natural, the Armed Forces shall: – Alone and together with allies, secure Norwegian sovereignty, Norwegian rights, interests and values, and preserve Norwegian freedom of action against military and other pressure

[452] – Through participation in multinational peace operations with an unambiguous anchoring in the UN Charter and international defense cooperation, contribute to peace, stability, enforcement of international law and respect for human rights, and prevent the use of force by states and non-state actors against Norwegian and international security. – Together with allies, contribute to the collective defense of Norway and other allies in accordance with our alliance commitments, and to meet various types of attacks and attacks to ensure Norwegian and collective security. – Contribute to safeguarding Norwegian societal security, saving lives and limiting the consequences of accidents, disasters, attacks and attacks from state and non-state actors

[453] The defense policy objectives are operationalized in the Armed Forces' tasks with the associated level of ambition, as well as in a number of fundamental principles for the organization of the Armed Forces

[454] The tasks of the Armed Forces

[455] The tasks of the Armed Forces can be summarized under the following headings

[456] To constitute a war-preventing threshold based on NATO membership To defend Norway and allies against serious threats, attacks and attacks, within the framework of NATO's collective defence To avert and handle incidents and security policy crises with national resources, including 2011–

[457] A defense for our time: Facilitate allied engagement if necessary Ensure a national decision-making basis through timely surveillance and intelligence Assert Norwegian sovereignty and sovereign rights Maintain the exercise of authority in limited areas Participate in multinational crisis management, including peace-support operations Contribute to international cooperation in the area of defense and security policy Contribute to safeguarding societal security and other key societal tasks Tasks 3–6 are tasks that must be able to be solved with national resources, and in principle without a particular degree of ongoing allied participation

[458] The tasks related to war prevention and defense of Norway and NATO must be solved in cooperation with others, and primarily with our allies in NATO

[459] This also applies to contributions to peace-supporting and stabilising efforts in the form of international operations, where Norway will make contributions within multilateral frameworks

[460] Task 8 is most often linked to cooperation with allies, but can also encompass purely bilateral assistance

[461] Task 9 is basically a national task, but may require cooperation and assistance across national borders

[462] The sizing of the Armed Forces depends on which capacities or structural elements the Armed Forces need, and how each capacity should be sized and organized

[463] Since several tasks require the same military capabilities, the capacity to solve several tasks in parallel is important in this assessment

[464] Basically, the main elements of the Defence structure are dimensioned to solve tasks

[465] At the same time, support for civil society must be included in the assessment of the organization and dimensioning of the individual capacities in the Defence Forces

[466] This is relevant, among other things, when designing dedicated missions, emergency preparedness orders, localization, requirements for training, exercises and practice, as well as the ability to collaborate with actors outside the defense sector

[467] Total defense means that society's total resources, both civilian and military, are used in the best possible way in crisis management in war and peace

[468] This involves mutual support and cooperation between the Armed Forces and civil society across the entire crisis spectrum

[469] The terrorist attacks on 22 July 2011 clearly highlighted the need for the Armed Forces to be prepared to provide assistance to civil society

[470] From an overall preparedness perspective, it is also important to maintain civil society's ability to support the Armed Forces in security crises

[471] The primary tasks of the Armed Forces are to assert Norway's sovereignty and defend the country against external attacks, while civilian authorities have the primary responsibility for safeguarding public security

[472] This is an established division of labor that has solid political and constitutional roots in Norway

[473] However, the Armed Forces' capabilities will at all times be adapted and used as appropriately as possible to support societal security in a broad sense, within the current resource framework and lines of responsibility

[474] Among the provisions that regulate civil-military cooperation, the assistance instructions are particularly central

[475] The instructions are now being reviewed again, among other things with a view to ensuring efficient procedures while maintaining responsibilities and legal frameworks

[476] Revision of the Norwegian Armed Forces' defense and emergency plans

[477] In the period after the end of the Cold War, the Norwegian Defence's operational planning and contingency arrangements related to security crises and war received modest attention, both nationally and in NATO

[478] The government has placed renewed focus on this type of planning work

[479] The work is not due to changes in the security policy picture, but reflects a need to update preparedness work for more extensive crises

[480] Central to the work is the review of the Armed Forces' operational planning related to the defense of Norway

[481] Basic principles for the organization of the Armed Forces

[482] Based on the framework set out above, the following fundamental principles shall form the basis for the organisation of the Armed Forces

[483] A modern, balanced in-bounds defense

[484] Norway needs a modern, alliance-adapted operational defense that can meet various challenges at home and abroad

[485] Such a defense must maintain high quality and possess high competence, flexibility, responsiveness, mobility and the ability to build up forces

[486] The Armed Forces must have the ability to cooperate effectively with allied forces, both to meet challenges in our immediate areas and to deliver significant contributions to international operations

[487] The Armed Forces should therefore, as far as possible, Prop

[488] A defense for our time must be adapted to NATO standards, concepts, procedures and force structure at all levels

[489] Ability for multinational cooperation

[490] The Armed Forces will continue their work to seek cost-effective solutions through multinational defense cooperation

[491] Military service and competence

[492] The defense of Norway is based on conscription

[493] Military service is a contract between citizens and the state that entails a duty of solidarity to stand together to protect our society, our democratic system and our common values

[494] Conscription is also central to ensuring the Armed Forces' broad recruitment of suitable personnel across social and cultural divides, while also ensuring that important peacekeeping tasks are carried out

[495] The first-aid service will be further developed and adapted to the operational defence forces' requirements for responsiveness, operational departments' need for flexibility and freedom of action, as well as increased requirements for competence and cost-effectiveness

[496] Those who perform their first service provide further recruitment grounds for officer training, enlistment or international service, and for the Army, after completing their service, they will be assigned to a period in the Army Reserve before being transferred to the Home Guard

[497] The Armed Forces shall emphasize the care of personnel participating in international operations and their loved ones, both before, during, and in the period after an operation

[498] Norway needs a defense that is flexible, robust and capable of handling various challenges

[499] The armed forces must be in continuous development and adaptation

[500] Cooperation with civil authorities

[501] The Armed Forces' cooperation with civilian actors shall be further developed to ensure efficiency based on good planning and functional procedures

[502] Well-coordinated and mutual cooperation across the entire crisis spectrum must be facilitated within the framework of total defence

[503] Where relevant, assistance to civil society shall be taken into account when designing the Armed Forces' capabilities

[504] The defense forces must be developed with a long-term perspective that ensures that financial resources, tasks and level of ambition are in line with each other

[505] Structure, organization and operational capability

[506] As an organization in continuous adaptation and modernization, the Armed Forces must further develop its structure and organization to meet current and future challenges

[507] This includes a strategy to address the sector's competence challenges, make necessary new acquisitions, including new combat aircraft, continue work to extract full operational effect from materiel systems that are being introduced, as well as organizational adjustments to ensure operational capability and availability

[508] Competence and personnel

[509] One of the defense sector's most important strategic challenges is the ability to attract, recruit, develop, employ and retain the right personnel with the right expertise

[510] The government has initiated strategic work to address the sector's competence challenges, where challenges and solutions must be seen in a holistic context

[511] The Government aims to present the results of this work to the Storting in the form of a report to the Storting by the end of the year

[512] The defense sector shall be a modern competence organization and continue the development from more traditional personnel management to strategic management of personnel development

[513] The sector should reflect societal developments to the greatest extent possible and contribute to them, for example through family and life-stage policies, inclusive working life and diversity

[514] The defense sector must recruit a diversity that meets the operational defense's need for a greater breadth of background, skills, characteristics and experiences among employees

[515] Not least, it is important to ensure that the sector is an attractive workplace for women

[516] The defense sector should be an attractive and safe workplace that protects employees and their ability to have the most normal family life possible

[517] This includes responsibility for looking after personnel before, during and after international operations

[518] The Government will further develop the work to strengthen the recognition and care of veterans in line with the Government's action plan "In service of Norway

[519] The defense of Norway is based on conscription as a solidary social contract

[567] Norway currently has a modern, well-balanced operational defense force, with the ability to carry out current tasks while at the same time investing in modern and future-oriented capabilities

[570] Good goal achievement has provided a good foundation for balanced and sustainable development

[586] Part I Frames and guides

[587] A defense for our time Security policy framework and trends 3.1 Norwegian security policy interests The main goal of security policy is to safeguard Norway's sovereignty, territorial integrity and political freedom of action

[588] Norway's fundamental security interest is to contribute to a multilateral world order under the UN with an emphasis on international law and human rights

[589] This is both an expression of international solidarity and the need for international regulation of relations between states

[590] Norway will also have an interest in contributing to stability outside the Euro-Atlantic area in the future

[591] For Norway, it is crucial to further develop and strengthen the transatlantic security community through NATO

[592] The alliance is the cornerstone of Norwegian security policy

[593] Norway's proximity to Russia means that it is in Norway's interest to contribute to good cooperation between Russia and the Western security community

[594] This is important both for international development in general and for stability in our immediate areas in particular

[595] The terrorist attacks on July 22, 2011 showed that Norway can also be exposed to extensive attacks on its own territory

[596] We must be prepared to avert and handle these, and the Armed Forces could have an important role in assisting the police

[597] Based on the fundamental security policy interests, Norway's main security policy objectives can be listed as follows: – To prevent war and the emergence of various threats to Norwegian and collective security. – To contribute to peace, stability and further development of a UN-led international legal order. – To safeguard Norwegian sovereignty, Norwegian rights, interests and values and protect Norwegian freedom of action against political, military and other pressure

[598] – Together with our allies, defend Norway and NATO against attacks and threats. – To secure society against attacks and threats from both state and non-state actors

[599] The armed forces are a fundamental and crucial security policy instrument

[600] The armed forces' ability to carry out their tasks constitutes a war-preventing threshold in that the costs of threatening or attacking Norwegian security become unacceptably high

[601] The formulation of Norwegian security policy is based on the assumption that the concept of security encompasses both state security, societal security and individual security

[602] The central purpose of security policy is to safeguard state security

[603] That is, to safeguard security needs related to the state's existence, sovereignty and integrity

[604] We also see challenges from non-state actors to societal security through, for example, terrorist attacks or attacks in the digital space

[605] Norwegian authorities place emphasis on safeguarding societal security where the safety of the civilian population and key societal functions and infrastructure may be challenged, but without the existence of the state being threatened

[606] International developments also show that greater emphasis is being placed on the protection of individuals

[607] An expression of this was the UN Security Council's emphasis on protecting the civilian population from abuses by their own authorities in Libya and Ivory Coast

[608] Geopolitical developments Globalization, the emergence of new great powers and the shift in economic power are strong trends in our time, which contribute to uncertainty about what security policy challenges Norway will face in the future

[609] The financial turmoil in recent years has reduced the ability of Western countries to handle new challenges

[610] Shift in global power relations and regional instability

[611] Prominent geopolitical developments of our time are increased rivalry between great powers and more emphasis on realpolitik

[612] Despite the fact that the United States is the world's leading power, emerging powers such as China in particular, but also Russia, India and Brazil, are contributing to a shift in power and a more fragmented world

[613] A defense of our time-honored global order

[614] The majority of the emerging powers are democracies

[615] Some, however, are characterized by a combination of authoritarian rule, market economy and strengthened military capability

[616] These represent an alternative to the Western democratic value system that may be attractive to other states

[617] Norway wants to develop contact with emerging powers to promote Norwegian interests and values, including democracy, international law and human rights

[618] Rivalry between great powers can put international law and multilateral solutions under pressure

[619] The coming years will likely be decisive in determining whether we move towards a world dominated by rival great powers or multilateralism and international cooperation

[620] The development will be important for global stability, and will also affect the situation in Norway's immediate vicinity

[621] Asia's growing influence has meant that the world's economic center of gravity is shifting from the West to the Pacific region

[622] The relationship between the United States and China will have a decisive impact on the level of international tension

[623] The relationship is characterized by both mutual economic dependence and increasing rivalry

[624] China is today the world's second largest economy and the world's largest exporting nation

[625] The United States remains a leader in terms of global political and military influence

[626] However, China's economic growth lays the foundation for a comprehensive modernization of the country's military forces

[627] China seeks to reduce the United States' lead in important military-strategic areas, such as outer space and the development of an ocean-going navy

[628] The United States is therefore turning more attention to Asia and the Pacific region, with the result that Europe receives less attention

[629] We are seeing a development where both China and Russia, as veto powers in the UN, are distancing themselves from the West on issues of great importance for international stability and the protection of human rights

[630] The world is experiencing widespread economic turmoil

[631] The economic problems in the United States, the euro area and several Asian countries are linked, among other things, to a large debt burden

[632] The weakened financial strength in Europe and the United States has led to cuts in public spending

[633] This will result in reduced military capacity for Norway's most important ally

[634] The United States is planning major reductions in defense spending in the coming years

[635] Larger European NATO countries, such as Germany and the United Kingdom, are also facing extensive cuts in military spending

[636] The United States has recently accounted for about three-quarters of total defense spending in NATO, but has warned European allies that they cannot expect the United States to cover an equal share of the costs of defending Europe in the future

[637] In addition, cuts in welfare measures and high unemployment have led to the emergence of extremist political movements that may represent a challenge to cohesion in the EU and NATO

[638] Another prominent development is the risk of instability in certain regions

[639] The Middle East and North Africa represent a belt of regional instability that can have ripple effects

[640] Since the spring of 2011, several countries in this area have undergone upheavals in the form of popular uprisings and regime changes

[641] A development towards pluralistic societies in this part of the world represents an important step forward that must be welcomed

[642] However, the development of more democratic forms of government will take time and may result in relapses in the form of new totalitarian regimes and religious fanaticism

[643] The transition phase could be violent and create a need for involvement from the international community

[644] The proximity to NATO countries in the south makes it important for the alliance to monitor developments closely

[645] NATO and Norway have devoted great attention to the Balkans since the 1990s

[646] Although Afghanistan has been a higher priority in recent years, the need for international attention to the Balkans is still present

[647] Most of the Balkan states are in the process of integrating into Euro-Atlantic institutions, but in Bosnia-Herzegovina and Kosovo the situation appears fragile due to, among other things, high unemployment, organized crime, a difficult economic situation and an unstable political landscape

[648] The Caucasus region is also characterized by unrest, frozen conflicts and growing contradictions

[649] Strategic supply lines, energy security and maritime security

[650] Modern societies are vulnerable as a result of greater dependence on strategic lines of communication, energy supplies, and information and computer technology for trade and communication

[651] Loss of critical infrastructure can have major ripple effects

[652] Access to free use of global commons such as international sea areas, international airspace, outer space and digital space is therefore important for most countries

[653] A disruption in communication lines can be a threat to both social and national security

[654] NATO's role in energy security is confirmed in the Strategic Concept, which primarily focuses on the protection of energy-related infrastructure and supply lines

[655] For Norway, which pro

[656] A defense for our time and supplier of oil and gas to the European continent, this is of great importance

[657] As a maritime nation, Norway has vital interests related to the freedom of the seas and the safety of commercial shipping

[658] In parts of the world, piracy is a threat to free movement in international waters

[659] Piracy has increased in scale in recent years and has challenged the international community with regard to effective countermeasures

[660] Norwegian shipping has also been affected

[661] Contributions to preventing and reducing piracy and to proper criminal prosecution are therefore important for Norwegian authorities

[662] Proliferation of weapons of mass destruction, disarmament and arms control NATO's Strategic Concept from 2010 commits the alliance to the goal of facilitating a world without nuclear weapons

[663] The spread of weapons of mass destruction (WMD – chemical, biological and nuclear weapons) to new states is a persistent threat to international security and stability

[664] The entire non-proliferation regime (Non Proliferation Treaty – NPT) is under increasing pressure

[665] This is particularly due to Iran and North Korea, which have long been a cause for concern

[666] Iran has the capacity to enrich uranium for weapons purposes

[667] The purpose of Iran's nuclear program is unknown, but it raises serious concerns that hidden facilities have been revealed and that the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) is denied access to the country's facilities

[668] Iran's willingness to sell technology and equipment to other countries is also worrying

[669] North Korea is a source of concern due to its unpredictable behavior combined with its nuclear capability, which has been demonstrated through test explosions

[670] Several countries that are in the process of acquiring nuclear weapons have also made significant progress in developing missile technology

[671] Iran is believed to have ballistic missiles with a range sufficient to reach NATO countries in southeastern Europe

[672] Iran also has a program that could provide the capacity to manufacture intercontinental ballistic missiles (ICBMs) that can reach all of Europe

[673] North Korea is developing missile technology that can be used to reach targets in the United States

[674] Developments in North Korea and Iran represent a risk of regional instability in both East Asia and the Middle East, and may also threaten global stability

[675] This development is much of the reason why NATO is emphasizing the introduction of missile defense

[676] Russia and the United States possess the bulk of the world's nuclear weapons arsenals

[677] It is therefore important that these countries follow up on their obligations under the NPT to reduce their nuclear weapons stockpiles

[678] In April 2010, the two countries signed a new START agreement

[679] New Strategic Arms Reduction Treaty

[680] This came into force in February 2011, replacing the previous START agreement which expired in 2011. In the new agreement, the United States and Russia commit to reducing offensive strategic nuclear weapons to 1,550 warheads each within seven years

[681] The government welcomes the New START Agreement as a concrete contribution to limiting strategic nuclear weapons

[682] American authorities have signaled a desire to continue negotiating with Russia on further reductions

[683] For Norway, it is important that such negotiations also include shorter-range nuclear weapons, which are a particular challenge in our immediate vicinity and in Europe

[684] For Norway, it is also important that the work on Confidence and Security Building Measures (CSBM) is taken forward within the OSCE framework

[685] The importance of such measures is reinforced by the fact that the future of the Conventional Forces Europe (CFE) Treaty is highly uncertain after Russia suspended it

[686] The world community faces a persistent and serious terrorist threat

[687] Terrorists employ a wide range of attack methods including explosives and small arms, suicide attacks and kidnappings

[688] Terrorist attacks using so-called dirty bombs cannot be ruled out either

[689] The attacks are directed against gatherings of people, symbolic and political targets, and economic interests

[690] Recent years show a trend where the main purpose is to cause as much damage and loss of life as possible, and where initial massive bombing attacks are often followed by other forms of violence

[691] The terrorist attack in Norway on July 22, 2011 confirms that the complexity of the terrorist threat has increased

[692] Attacks can come from both outside and inside, and from different environments or individuals

[693] Groups and individuals with different political or religious positions can plan or carry out terrorist acts

[694] Militant Islamist networks linked to or inspired by al-Qaeda's ideology continue to pose one of the most serious threats

[695] Such groups are strongest in Pakistan, Afghanistan, Yemen, Iraq and Somalia, but also have a presence in other countries in the Middle East and Southeast Asia

[696] In the border areas between- Prop

[697] In Pakistan and Afghanistan, people from European countries are also trained, and some of them return with the intention of carrying out attacks in Europe

[698] The terrorist threat has led to increased emphasis on societal security both in Norway and in the West in general

[699] Despite the attack in Norway, the London bombings in July 2005, the Madrid bombings in 2004, and attacks in Russia, a number of planned attacks have also been revealed and thwarted

[700] The Norwegian Intelligence Service works actively to uncover international terrorism that poses a danger to Europe

[701] In Norway, terrorist attacks are initially considered serious crimes, but they can take forms that result in them being considered armed attacks in accordance with the UN Charter

[702] The extensive terrorist attacks of recent years show that state security can also be threatened

[703] Threats in the digital space

[704] Norwegian societal and state security is also challenged by threats related to the use of digital technology and the ability to disseminate and control information

[705] Attacks in digital space, also known as “cyberspace”, are one of the fastest growing threats to individuals, businesses and public institutions

[706] The attacks can come from both state and non-state actors, for example from other countries' military defense, intelligence services, organized crime, terrorist and extremist groups, competing businesses and individual hackers

[707] The most serious threat comes from states

[708] Identifying the source of such attacks can be a challenge

[709] Attacks in the digital space can primarily affect societal security by disabling critical functions

[710] Depending on the scope and objectives, digital attacks can also threaten national security

[711] For example, advanced operations could weaken military command and control systems

[712] Low costs and the ability to operate covertly make the digital space an attractive arena

[713] Most of the incidents in recent years have been espionage attacks and not sabotage attacks

[714] The attacks therefore primarily represent a threat to information security, but the development may move towards sabotaging critical infrastructure

[715] The defense sector is also affected by digital attacks and must deal with its own vulnerability

[716] NATO is meeting the growing threat by supporting member states' efforts, centralizing the alliance's own digital protection measures, and improving security at the interface between NATO's and member states' information infrastructure

[717] International law and the digital space

[718] Digital attacks will be covered by national legislation in peacetime

[719] If the attack originates in another country, international criminal law and international treaties, such as the Council of Europe Convention on Cybercrime, will apply

[720] However, a digital attack against another state could, depending on the circumstances, also be considered an unlawful use of force under Article 2 of the UN Charter and thus be contrary to general international law

[721] Important points in assessing whether the prohibition of force, and thus a state's sovereignty, has been violated

[722] is the purpose and legitimacy of the attack, as well as the strength and consequences of the attack

[723] A digital attack could also trigger a state's right to self-defense under the UN Charter's article

[724] The threshold for this is, however, high, and will typically only apply where the state is exposed to a large-scale attack directed at critical infrastructure, or if the attack causes significant loss of life or material damage

[725] If the attack is not serious enough to trigger the right of self-defense, the affected state will still have the opportunity to implement other countermeasures that do not involve the use of force

[726] A complicating factor is that it is often very difficult to trace the origin of the attack, while the burden of proof lies with the state that wishes to take countermeasures

[727] Humanitarian law applies in principle to digital warfare

[728] Digital weapons are not in themselves in violation of humanitarian law, as long as a distinction is made between protected civilians and objects on the one hand, and lawful military targets on the other

[729] Despite the fact that digital warfare, due to its unique nature, raises a number of complicated legal issues, this does not mean that current international law is insufficient to solve the challenges

[730] The establishment of new international law instruments is therefore considered neither necessary nor desirable

[731] Globalization, strategic shocks and climate change

[732] Our time is characterized by increasing interaction and stronger interdependence between states

[733] For Norway, it is beneficial and valuable that goods, services, information and ideas spread quickly across national borders

[734] At the same time, globalization contributes to new security challenges, partly due to the uneven distribution of the economic benefits of globalization

[735] The interdependence between countries and less clear boundaries between them 2011–

[736] National and international events contribute to the fact that events far away can have immediate and serious consequences for Norwegian security

[737] Various security policy and technological trends provide some indication of future developments

[738] Nevertheless, we cannot rule out strategic shocks in the form of unexpected natural or man-made upheavals that could have major consequences

[739] Examples of such extensive events may include regional unrest or war, regime collapse, major terrorist attacks, nuclear accidents, collapses in international financial systems, digital system collapses in key societal functions, pandemics and extreme geophysical phenomena

[740] Such shocks can threaten both societal security and state security

[741] Despite the fact that it is not possible to guard against strategic shocks, it is important to develop the most robust security mechanisms and flexible civilian and military capacities possible

[742] For vulnerable modern societies, participation in an effective and reliable alliance provides increased resilience

[743] Global developments are characterized by environmental challenges and climate change, including global warming

[744] The long-term consequences may include higher temperatures and rising sea levels, increased erosion, flooding, deforestation and desertification

[745] At the same time, competition for strategic resources such as fossil energy, freshwater, minerals and marine resources is increasing

[746] Multilateral security cooperation

[747] The security challenges of our time emphasize the importance of the UN as an international framework for a multilateral world order based on international law and human rights

[748] Solving global challenges requires that the major powers be able to stand together on important security issues

[749] However, there is a danger that the vested interests of major powers could contribute to weakening the UN's position

[750] This is also a reminder that the UN will become more important for small states like Norway

[751] For Norway, it is therefore important that the UN's role as a multilateral forum for dialogue, cooperation and conflict resolution is clear and strong

[752] The UN and the Security Council are key providers of the legality and legitimacy of the use of military force

[753] Military peacekeeping operations are among the UN's foremost and most sought-after tools in its work for peace and security

[754] The number of personnel in peacekeeping operations for the UN has increased significantly over the past ten years, from about 20,000 in 2000 to

[755] Of these, about 85,000 are military personnel

[756] Countries in the south bear a large part of the challenges in the field under demanding conditions

[757] Most of today's conflicts are intrastate and are often characterized by weak state power, multiple warring parties and violence against the civilian population

[758] For UN peacekeeping operations, the protection of civilians has therefore become an increasingly important task

[759] This requires robust and well-qualified military and police forces and extensive cooperation with national authorities, organizations and the UN in general

[761] The mandates associated with the operations in Libya and Côte d'Ivoire in 2011 were historic because they authorized the use of military force by the international community to protect civilians from abuses by their own authorities

[762] The mandates were rooted in the principles adopted by the UN in 2005 regarding the international community's right to intervene in the internal affairs of states to prevent such abuses

[763] The popular uprisings in North Africa and the Middle East from the spring of 2011 may lead to the UN taking on a new role in these areas, given that the Security Council can agree on such an engagement

[764] Military force is not a panacea that can solve all security challenges, but must be assessed in each individual case and requires a UN mandate

[988] Priorities in Norwegian security and defense policy

[989] The security policy environment shows that Norway faces complex challenges

[990] Norway is not currently facing a direct military threat

[991] The general uncertainty nevertheless means that we cannot rule out deteriorations in the security situation

[995] In addition, globalization and the breadth of asymmetric threats represent a growing challenge to societal security, and in the worst case, also to state security

[996] It is therefore important to pursue a long-term and predictable security and defense policy

[998] The Norwegian Defence Force also has an important role in contributing to societal security within the framework of total defence
