[1014] This applies, for example, to support the development of NATO's missile defense in Europe and measures against attacks in digital space

[1015] Both are included in NATO's new strategic concept

[1016] The Norwegian Armed Forces shall both further develop their own defence capabilities in the digital space and contribute to NATO's robustness, including by contributing to NATO's collective efforts to counter such attacks

[1017] Thirdly, Norway must actively support the implementation of NATO's new command structure

[1018] In order to achieve a closer bond between FOH and allied commands, Norway will particularly prioritize: contributing to increased situational understanding by communicating situational awareness, assessments and analyses, contributing to setting exercises within its own area of operations in a NATO context and contributing to increasing the capacity for crisis management by preparing plans and clarifying roles already in peacetime

[1019] Fourthly, it will be necessary to facilitate the transfer and reception of allied reinforcements to Norway

[1020] This includes helping to renew the arrangements for Norwegian host country support and further developing the capacity to receive allied reinforcements

[1021] A prominent element of the alliance affiliation is education, training and exercises

[1022] Here, NATO's Joint Warfare Center (JWC) in Stavanger will become an effective and useful resource for the alliance, especially after Afghanistan

[1023] The Armed Forces shall facilitate this type of allied activity in the north

[1024] Norway represents a unique area for military training activities and we will continue to emphasize annual comprehensive joint operational exercises

[1025] The exercises should include the upper reaches of the crisis spectrum and the transfer of allied forces

[1026] Prioritizing national measures

[1027] A prerequisite for NATO's reinforcement role in Norway to be credible is that we ourselves actively contribute to the defense of our own areas and to safeguarding our own interests

[1028] Firstly, emphasis will be placed on maintaining a high level of ambition for key national tasks such as surveillance, intelligence, assertion of sovereignty and the exercise of authority

[1029] This requires a solid military presence in the north

[1030] Such a visible presence contributes to safeguarding allied and Norwegian interests and to stability in the surrounding areas

[1031] The restructuring of the Armed Forces in recent decades has led to efficiency improvements and concentration in the Armed Forces' logistics and base structure

[1032] The government's policy is that this should not result in reduced operational activity in the north

[1033] As part of the situational understanding, increased emphasis will also be placed on in-depth expertise on developments in Russia

[1034] Secondly, we will prioritize the ability to handle minor security incidents and crises nationally

[1035] The ability to respond quickly in a crisis situation in the north will also be further developed, and the introduction of new combat aircraft will help strengthen capacity and presence in the north

[1036] For a long period, NATO has focused on challenges outside its own area of responsibility, which has led to a deprioritization of planning for the home regions

[1037] In Norway too, the planning works have received little attention

[1038] Norway is now revitalizing its own defense and emergency planning to facilitate force building and effective crisis management in the event of security policy crises

[1039] There is also a need for better coordination between national and allied planning agencies

[1040] Thirdly, today's security challenges mean that increased emphasis must be placed on total defence and civil-military cooperation

[1041] Terrorism and digital attacks primarily affect societal security, but can also affect state security

[1042] Furthermore, Norway cannot rule out traditional challenges to Norwegian national security

[1043] The modernized total defense concept is founded on mutual support and cooperation between the Armed Forces and civil society

[1044] In recent years, attention has been focused on the Armed Forces' assistance to civil society

[1045] This tendency was further highlighted as a result of the terrorist attacks on July

[1046] At the same time, it is important to emphasize that in times of crisis and war, the Norwegian Defence Forces will be dependent on support from civil society in several areas in order to be able to carry out their tasks

[1047] In Norway, the judicial authorities and the police have primary responsibility for combating terrorism

[1048] Emphasis is placed on the Armed Forces' ability to support civilian authorities

[1049] A defense for our time

[1050] Emphasizing multinational defense cooperation and military diplomacy

[1051] The need for multinational cooperation has been reinforced as a result of the financial crisis and the subsequent reduction in defense budgets of the largest NATO countries

[1052] Better cooperation within NATO as a whole and regionally between member states and partner countries is necessary to maintain the breadth of the defense structure, especially for smaller states

[1053] Particularly among the European allies, it is important to increase the scope of multinational cooperation to increase the European defense effort and contribute to better burden sharing across the Atlantic

[1054] On the European side, the Nordic countries and the other countries in the Northern Group are our natural cooperation partners in this context, and these will be given special priority

[1055] Norway will also develop security policy ties through confidence-building military diplomacy

[1056] Through, among other things, high-level defense-related visits, dialogue on security challenges and port visits, Norway wishes to contribute to stable and peaceful development both in the Euro-Atlantic area and in other areas and countries of interest to Norway

[1057] Contribution to international operations Participation in international operations will continue to be an important part of Norwegian security policy

[1058] Norwegian contributions abroad have in recent years been recognized by the UN, NATO and the EU

[1059] Norwegian military involvement abroad shall primarily be aimed at promoting and protecting Norwegian interests where these are directly or indirectly affected

[1060] The increased challenges in Norwegian areas may mean that, in a given situation, Norway will have to prioritize its own areas over international operations

[1061] Challenges in Norwegian local areas indicate that we must at all times consider what emphasis should be placed on the ability to handle potential crises at home

[1062] Norwegian authorities place great emphasis on ensuring that the conditions for the use of military force are met before international operations are launched

[1063] The use of military force requires anchoring in the UN Charter

[1064] It gives the operation legality and legitimacy

[1065] The use of military force also requires that the forces operate in accordance with international law, and within the framework of any given guidelines for the use of force (Rules of Engagement — ROE

[1066] Command and control for the force must specify clear lines of command and responsibility and provide Norwegian authorities with sufficient insight into operations and management of Norwegian units

[1067] In general, Norway's ambitions for engagement abroad mean that the Armed Forces must be prepared to contribute forces to operations, primarily under the auspices of the UN and NATO, but to a certain extent also under the auspices of the EU

[1068] Contributions must be based on reasonable burden sharing

[1069] Norwegian departments must be well trained and equipped for the missions they undertake

[1070] In the coming years, we will probably see a smaller scale of heavy operations with land forces

[1071] This is due, among other things, to the escalation in Afghanistan, general war fatigue among major allies, and general geopolitical developments

[1072] The Armed Forces should continue to be able to contribute to the full range of international operations

[1073] It includes preventive stabilization operations, peacekeeping operations and peace-making operations

[1074] New types of operations such as anti-piracy operations must also be emphasized

[1075] Conflict-affected countries often have a weak tradition of political dialogue and negotiated solutions, and lack elementary social institutions

[1076] Military efforts must therefore be part of a comprehensive approach, which includes, among other things, diplomatic and economic instruments

[1077] The armed forces must be able to be made available at short notice, but perseverance in maintaining alliance contributions over time has proven important and demanding

[1078] Considerations for endurance and the ability to regenerate forces indicate that we strive to distribute the burden of participating in international operations across different parts of the defense structure

[1079] Norway's main priority in Afghanistan will be to contribute to NATO's strategy for transferring responsibility for security in the country to Afghan authorities (transition

[1080] Norway will continue its work to strengthen the UN's peacekeeping efforts and prioritize UN-initiated operations

[1081] As a supplement to participation in international operations, Norway emphasizes contributing to Defense and Security Sector Reform (DSSR) in vulnerable regions

[1082] Such work can be considered partly as follow-up of countries in regions where Norway and NATO have been engaged in military operations and partly as general community building in states with development potential

[1083] Implications for the application and design of the Armed Forces

[1084] The analysis of Norway's security policy environment and interests provides the following overall guidelines for defense policy

[1085] A defense for our time – The main goal of defense policy in the coming years will be to further develop operational defense with the aim of solving tasks both at home and abroad

[1086] The Armed Forces must be able to meet complex challenges to Norwegian national and societal security

[1087] The defense should also be designed to contribute actively to NATO's relevance and effectiveness, both in the alliance's area and in other parts of the world. – Collective defense means that cooperation and interoperability with allies and partners should be given great importance

[1088] The development of the Armed Forces shall be based on NATO standards and strength targets

[1089] The Armed Forces shall contribute to linking NATO to Norway by facilitating allied training and exercises in Norway, regular allied presence and credible reception apparatus and host country support for allied reinforcements. – The Armed Forces must pay more attention to being able to handle a security crisis in our immediate areas

[1090] Norway must be able to handle limited crises and incidents alone, but above a certain level they must be handled in cooperation with allies

[1091] In this context, it is important that the Armed Forces also contribute to preventing conflict

[1092] The Armed Forces must therefore, through its roles and overall activities, constitute a war-preventing threshold. – The Armed Forces must be able to contribute across the entire spectrum of conflicts, from incidents, via crises, to war operations with allies

[1093] A prerequisite for this is that the Armed Forces consist of a balanced and modern defence structure consisting of land, sea and air assets

[1094] Modern combat aircraft are a prerequisite for maintaining Norway's ability to react quickly over long distances and safeguard Norwegian interests at home and abroad. – In order to safeguard Norwegian interests in our immediate vicinity, the Armed Forces must also maintain a high level of ambition for a number of ongoing peacetime tasks such as surveillance, intelligence, assertion of sovereignty and exercise of authority

[1095] The development of the Armed Forces must take into account that climate change in the Arctic may lead to increased requirements for range and presence within a larger sea area in the north. – The Armed Forces must have the ability to react quickly to safeguard Norwegian interests in their own areas and nearby areas, and to be able to react quickly together with allies in operations abroad

[1096] At the same time, Norwegian forces must have sufficient endurance both to handle crises in our immediate area and to be able to contribute abroad together with allies over time

[1097] These requirements assume that the Armed Forces have a certain volume

[1098] Conscription will continue to be a cornerstone of future defense

[1099] Renewal of both defense and emergency plans is important for responsiveness and endurance. – The Armed Forces shall strengthen the ability for preventive security and contribute to national and allied defense capabilities within the digital space

[1100] – Increased emphasis should be placed on total defense as security challenges can affect both state and societal security

[1101] Total defence encompasses mutual support and cooperation between the Armed Forces and civil society across the entire crisis spectrum from peace, via security policy crises to war

[1102] Mutual civil-military support and coordination must facilitate the most efficient use of resources, both in prevention, emergency planning and operational efforts. – Norway must be able to make significant contributions to international operations, under the auspices of the UN, NATO and, to some extent, the EU

[1103] The Armed Forces must be able to cooperate with allies and partners in the full spectrum of international operations, including preventive, peacekeeping and peace-making operations, in addition to new types of operations such as anti-piracy operations. – Norway shall develop the ability to collect and analyze information of importance for security policy developments

[1104] The Armed Forces must therefore place great emphasis on intelligence and analysis of developments both in our immediate areas and in areas where Norwegian forces are involved. – For Norway's security policy credibility, it is important to maintain a long-term balance between the Armed Forces' resources and tasks

[1105] An important tool for maintaining a balanced defense structure is increased emphasis on multinational defense cooperation

[1106] Norway must place the main emphasis on cooperation that underpins the ability to operate together with other NATO countries

[1107] A defense for our time

[1108] The armed forces are an integrated part of society and interact with their surroundings

[1109] The ability to capture new trends and developments that may impact the Armed Forces' organization, priorities and activities is becoming increasingly important, as interaction with society at large is increasing

[1110] This chapter points to some societal, economic, technological and environmental developments that have, or may have, consequences for the Armed Forces and defense planning

[1111] These developments must be seen in the context of the general security policy developments in Norway's surroundings, which are described in chapter

[1112] Together with Chapter 3, Chapter 4 forms a framework of premises for the development and organization of the Norwegian Defence Forces

[1113] The Armed Forces depend on long-term planning

[1114] Developments such as demographic changes, emphasis on real gender equality, increased civil-military interaction and multinational cooperation, increased need for technological expertise and stricter requirements for the environment and climate emissions are all trends and factors that affect the Armed Forces

[1115] The same applies to economic trends and competition for public funds

[1116] Strict requirements are imposed on sound management and transparency regarding the Armed Forces' activities

[1117] A holistic approach, where measures and instruments are put into context and adapted to future challenges, is necessary for the further development of the Armed Forces

[1118] The Armed Forces in Society

[1119] The armed forces have broad support among the Norwegian population

[1120] A large majority of public opinion has supported the maintenance of a strong defense, even after the clear threat picture of the Cold War was replaced by more complex challenges

[1121] Support for the Armed Forces is demonstrated, among other things, through a long-term, steady and high level of funding for defense purposes

[1122] The Government places great emphasis on the Armed Forces proving themselves worthy of this trust, not only by managing allocated resources in the best possible way, but also by being aware of their responsibility as a significant social actor with activities that affect many people throughout the country

[1123] Directly and indirectly, the activities of the defense sector create a number of societal ripple effects – many positive and some challenging

[1124] The defense sector is a large workplace; in some places, the dominant employer in the local community

[1125] Furthermore, the defense sector contributes to the development of new technology and expertise, which is important for general innovation and expertise development in society at large

[1126] The armed forces are also an important carrier of culture, a transmitter of tradition and a guardian of history, and stand as a symbolic expression of our will to assert our national sovereignty and independence

[1127] At the same time, the Armed Forces can impose burdens on the surrounding society

[1128] Defence activities require access to large areas

[1129] Operations, training and exercise activities cause noise and other external impacts on the environment

[1130] The Armed Forces' host municipalities across the country deserve recognition for the efforts they make to facilitate the Armed Forces' activities

[1131] At the same time, the Armed Forces' organization has been reduced in size in recent decades, and as a consequence, the Armed Forces are represented in fewer places in the country

[1132] In addition, fewer people than before are completing their first-time service

[1133] This means that fewer and fewer people have a direct connection to the Armed Forces and its activities as an employer or in the local community

[1134] This may contribute to reducing knowledge about and understanding of the defense sector and the role of the Armed Forces in society, thereby weakening the recruitment base

[1135] It is very important that the Armed Forces appear as a visible, open and modern organization, and further develop the interface with civil society, to ensure access to expertise and resources

[1136] All of this means that the Armed Forces are in a relationship of mutual influence with other parts of society, both nationally and locally

[1137] The organisation of the armed forces must therefore take into account a broad spectrum of societal developments

[1138] A defense for our time Civil-military interdependence

[1139] With a complex threat landscape, where the distinction between military and civilian means of power and resources has become more complex, good cooperation between civilian and military actors is crucial

[1140] Society has become more vulnerable as a result of centralization, specialization, and dependence on information and communication technology

[1141] At the same time, society is expected to function approximately normally while a crisis is being handled

[1142] Despite the fact that the Armed Forces' main rationale is to defend the country against external aggression or pressure, the ability to contribute to societal security is therefore becoming increasingly important for the Armed Forces

[1143] In addition, the Armed Forces have become more integrated with civil society when it comes to the provision of expertise, delivery of goods and services, and technology

[1144] This further reinforces the need for cooperation, based on mutual understanding of roles and responsibilities developed through joint training and interaction between military and civilian actors

[1145] Participation in international operations has in recent years also created increasing demands for cooperation between the Armed Forces and civilian actors

[1146] When the international community becomes involved in a conflict area, it is with the goal of promoting peaceful and stable development

[1147] This requires integrated and coordinated efforts in several areas, where military efforts are only one of several instruments

[1148] Particularly in the UN context, emphasis has therefore been placed on cooperation between, on the one hand, civilian assistance and advice to contribute to economic development and good governance, and, on the other hand, military assistance to create security for the population and facilitate peaceful development

[1149] Norway supports this approach and sees integrated peace operations as a prerequisite for achieving positive development in conflict areas

[1150] At the same time, Norway has emphasized that military forces should not take over, or compete with, civilian aid organizations in carrying out tasks related to civilian assistance

[1151] Particular caution must be exercised in operations where Norway can be considered a party, such as in Afghanistan

[1152] In some cases, however, there may also be a need in such operations for military actors to carry out tasks that are in principle civilian, if other actors are unable to provide the necessary assistance

[1153] In pure peacekeeping operations where Norway must be considered a third party, the scope for providing assistance to civil society is somewhat greater

[1154] Integrated peace operations require a high level of attention to roles and responsibilities

[1155] There is a clear trend towards increased use of civilian actors in support of international military operations

[1156] The use of civilian partners has been increasing, particularly in logistics and supplies

[1157] Since the Armed Forces in international operations collaborate closely with allies and partners, such events will often be part of a collaboration between several military contributors to the operation

[1158] In such cases, the Armed Forces must emphasize that civilian companies that assist a military operation offer their employees satisfactory wages, working conditions and personal security

[1159] A further challenge is that some of the Armed Forces' partners in international operations also use civilian suppliers for tasks related to security, protection, bodyguard services and other missions that could potentially involve the use of force

[1160] The Norwegian Armed Forces do not use such private security companies, but will be able to operate in a broader context where other partners use services from such private actors in the same operation

[1161] Interaction between civilians and military personnel in a conflict situation in such fields places great demands on orderliness and clarity in relation to roles and responsibilities

[1162] This requires thorough consideration of legal and ethical issues, among other things

[1163] In the future, the Armed Forces will increasingly be able to meet such challenges in connection with international operations

[1164] The increasing complexity of the interaction between military and civilian actors places great demands on competence and awareness among Norwegian personnel, especially in management functions

[1165] Personnel in relevant functions must be prepared for the challenges that may arise, and have clear guidelines for how to handle them

[1166] The authorities at home in Norway, for their part, will emphasize the ability to guide personnel serving abroad when the need arises to provide guidance in handling the issues that may arise

[1167] Multicultural and a more diverse society and working life

[1168] Society is characterized by an ever-increasing diversity: ethnic, cultural, religious, linguistic, knowledge-based and experiential

[1169] At the same time, family structures and work patterns are becoming more flexible and varied, which places greater demands on organizations' flexibility as employers and their ability to individually adapt working conditions

[1170] The Norwegian Armed Forces aim to reflect the population's cultural, ethnic, religious and competence diversity to a greater extent in order to ensure legitimacy and credibility in society

[1171] Diversity and for- 2011–

[1172] A defense of our time and standing for other cultures is an important competence in itself

[1173] The composition of the population is therefore of great importance to the Armed Forces

[1174] Changes in family and work patterns, and the development towards a more multicultural society, are placing new demands on the Armed Forces in terms of recruitment, equality, diversity and family policy

[1175] These issues are further described in Chapter 9. Increased level of knowledge and requirements for competence

[1176] A higher level of education and increased access to information means that the level of knowledge in the population is constantly increasing

[1177] This leads to employees making greater demands on the content of their work and their ability to influence the work situation

[1178] At the same time, technological developments mean that personnel must operate and maintain increasingly advanced equipment, which places greater demands on specialized expertise and adapted education

[1179] It is crucial for the Armed Forces' further development to ensure good and comprehensive competence management, in order to optimally utilize personnel resources and be able to compete for competence in an increasingly competitive labor market

[1180] This also applies to the recruitment of conscripts

[1181] The Armed Forces must become better at applying expertise developed by others, and a two-way flow of expertise must be facilitated between the sector and society at large

[1182] At the same time, the Armed Forces are dependent on a certain amount of expertise that is very rarely available in the market

[1183] The Armed Forces, the Labor Market and an Aging Population

[1184] The military recruits a lot of manpower

[1185] Norway is currently a country with very low unemployment, which is very positive

[1186] The degree of tightness in the labor market could affect the Armed Forces' ability to recruit and retain manpower

[1187] The tightness of the labor market is affected in the short term by economic conditions and in the longer term by demographic developments

[1188] In isolation, an increased average age in the population tends towards increased scarcity

[1189] On the other hand, after 2004, when we gained a common labor market with countries in Central and Eastern Europe, Norway has become part of a large European labor market and labor immigration has contributed significantly to increasing the supply of labor

[1190] Reforms in working life, especially the pension reform, are also intended to increase the supply of labor

[1191] The tightness in the labor market will also be affected by the fact that fiscal and monetary policy aims to stabilize wage and cost developments by adjusting labor demand to supply

[1192] In a situation with high employment and low unemployment, the Defence Force will also face challenges in attracting and retaining labour

[1193] Economic developments Large parts of the world are affected by the international economic downturn resulting from the financial crisis

[1194] This has led to a significant weakening of public finances in a number of industrialized countries

[1195] Large budget deficits and increasing government debt have led to questions being raised about whether developments in these countries are sustainable over time

[1196] Although several countries have implemented necessary measures to reduce their budget deficits, there are still major financial challenges in several countries

[1197] Calculations from the OECD show that member countries as a group must tighten their budgets significantly over the next 15 years to stabilize gross debt as a share of GDP

[1198] Further tightening is needed to reduce the debt ratio to the same level as before the financial crisis

[1199] Norway, on the other hand, has experienced renewed economic growth since the summer of 2009 and employment has picked up

[1200] The economic turmoil following the financial crisis in 2008 has already affected the defense sector in many countries

[1201] Most of our NATO allies and partners are reducing their defense budgets

[1202] Several countries are forced to make extensive reorganizations and cuts in the defense sector to help reduce government budgets in the short term

[1203] Such a forced change may make it necessary to remove parts of the defense structure and thereby reduce operational capability

[1204] Among some of Norway's NATO allies, it has also been shown that short-term cuts have affected defense structures and operational capabilities in a way that has already had far-reaching consequences

[1205] A more long-term consequence of the tight economic situation is that planned investments in new military capabilities must be postponed or canceled

[1206] Overall, this development could affect our allies' ability to support Norway in both the short and long term. Norway is one of the few countries in Europe that has surpluses in its public budgets

[1207] In addition, Norway has high employment, and women's labor force participation is very high

[1208] This is one of the most important prerequisites for growth and prosperity in Norwegian society and, among other things, enables us to maintain a comprehensive, high-quality welfare state

[1209] A defense for our time: the turmoil in the financial markets and general uncertainty about further economic developments, especially in the United States and Europe, may have ripple effects on the Norwegian economy

[1210] The uniquely Norwegian revenues from the oil and gas sector have a limited duration, while expenditures on pensions, health and care are increasing

[1211] In the longer term, Norway also faces major challenges in fiscal policy, partly as a result of an aging population

[1212] Allocations to the defense sector

[1213] Over the past few decades, the defense sector in most countries in Europe has received a decreasing share of the state budget compared to other public sectors

[1214] The great economic growth in Europe over the past twenty years has consequently been used for purposes other than defense

[1215] Of the NATO countries, only the United States and the United Kingdom have planned to significantly increase the priority given to the defense sector in the same period, measured as the defense sector's share of GDP

[1216] This is related, among other things, to large expenditures on international operations and the extensive warfare in Iraq and Afghanistan

[1217] However, we see that both the United States and the United Kingdom are now in the process of implementing some dramatic reductions in their defense structures

[1218] Among the emerging economies, China stands out as an economic power, which is reflected in the development of defense spending, see figure

[1219] Russia has kept the growth in its defense budget on par with other major powers despite somewhat weaker economic development over the past four years

[1220] The growth of China's military power has contributed to increased interest in Southeast Asia from countries such as the United States

[1221] Given Norway's strong economy, access to significant energy resources in combination with a potential weakening of allies' defense capabilities and reduced American interest in Europe, it is crucial for Norway to continue its commitment to a modern operational defense that represents a credible war prevention threshold

[1222] Reduced defense appropriations among allies are taking place at the same time as extensive restructuring needs for military organizations are emerging

[1223] This development is forcing an increased need for extensive multinational cooperation in several areas

[1224] Multinational cooperation can provide cost savings and/or increased operational effectiveness

[1225] It can also help maintain the breadth of existing military capabilities

[1226] Other related countries will view expanded defense cooperation as a strategy for dealing with a situation where cuts to defense budgets are necessary

[1227] Although Norway has increased its defense spending in recent years, Figure 4.1 The development of the defense budget compared with the development in allied countries, Russia and China

[1228] A defense for our time Sixth, we face many of the same challenges as other countries related to, among other things, increased costs for qualified labor, as well as increased costs related to defense technology and materiel

[1229] Consequently, Norway will benefit greatly from participating in multinational defense cooperation, among other things to be able to distribute investment and operating costs among several actors and achieve economies of scale

[1230] In addition, multinational cooperation can give Norway access to and control over capabilities that a small country cannot otherwise prioritize resources to either invest in, operate or maintain

[1236] The Norwegian Armed Forces have undergone extensive reorganization and modernization over the past decade

[1237] This has provided a more effective and timely defense

[1238] Compared to many of Norway's allies and partners, Norway is far ahead in restructuring and modernizing the Armed Forces

[1242] Technological developments

[1243] The Armed Forces are a technology-intensive organization

[1244] Technological development is a very important factor in the ongoing modernization and renewal of the Armed Forces

[1245] The Norwegian Armed Forces are currently at a very high level of quality, and many of our new capabilities are among the best that can be produced, and are thus adapted to today's challenges, both abroad and at home

[1246] This has led to the Armed Forces' new materiel systems having a greater effect, being less per- Figure 4.2 Developments in netted defence budgets measured in 2012 kroner, compensating for specific cost growth in the defence sector, (corrected for gross budgeting of Defence Construction from 2011 onwards

[1247] A defense for our time zone-intensive and provides better protection for personnel

[1248] Modern warfare demands the ability to operate in an integrated manner across defense branches and together with allies and partners

[1249] Technological developments have an impact on how operations are carried out

[1250] Modernization involves renewing equipment and improving working methods and operations

[1251] By using advanced technology, the Armed Forces will be able to solve tasks more effectively and with greater power, alone and together with allies and partners

[1252] Traditional platforms, weapon types, means of communication and sensors will also be part of the defense structure in the future

[1253] At the same time, developments will move towards greater use of smaller and more compact equipment

[1254] There are ever increasing demands and expectations for better personal protection, greater precision and lighter equipment, which is introducing new materials and information and communication technology into soldier equipment

[1255] Weapons systems have significantly increased precision, and development is now focusing on applying technologies, systems and platforms to new fields

[1256] This is an extension of the automation and miniaturization trends, including the introduction of unmanned platforms

[1257] In military operations, the Armed Forces use solutions developed in areas such as information and communication technology, biotechnology, energy technology and nanotechnology

[1258] This, together with advanced technological solutions such as unmanned systems and systems that can be operated from a long distance, is crucial for the effective implementation of network-based operations

[1259] The Government places great emphasis on the Armed Forces using new, advanced technological solutions in order to maintain a high level of operational capability and to keep personnel safe

[1260] Development is happening quickly

[1261] It is crucial to keep up with technological developments in order to continuously develop a relevant defense to meet changing defense and security challenges, including being able to create a war-preventing threshold

[1262] Experience shows that it is very demanding and costly to rebuild sufficient capacities if one has already fallen behind

[1263] A defense that continuously keeps up with and reflects technological developments is therefore fundamental to the Armed Forces' ability to perform its tasks

[1264] The development of network-based defense is a priority area

[1265] This involves the use of information technology to link capacities and actors together in a network, both across the branches of defense and at different levels in the organization

[1266] The aim is, among other things, to provide the most up-to-date and complete decision-making basis possible
