[2340] This concept is based on a multinational collaboration between user nations and industry, where the user nations and industry form long-term cooperative arrangements

[2424] Capability The Air Force's operational structure currently includes control and warning systems, combat aircraft, ground-based air defense, electronic warfare aircraft, VIP and calibration flights, maritime surveillance aircraft, maritime helicopters, tactical transport helicopters, tactical transport aircraft, base defense and rescue helicopters

[2425] The Air Force's operational capability is also a function of the base structure and logistical support

[2426] What is common to air forces is that missions are in most cases carried out within a joint operational framework

[2432] Operational management of air combat forces is currently handled centrally through the Armed Forces' operational headquarters in national operations, and through NATO's chain of command for the control and warning stations and combat aircraft on QRA readiness, as well as when air forces contribute abroad or in multinational operations in Norway

[2483] A defense for our time Changes related to the Air Force base and support structure

[2484] Norway has chosen the F-35 as its new fighter aircraft and this aircraft will, like the F-16, form the core of a system of systems around which the remaining air defense structure will be built

[2485] The F-35 has a significantly greater range of capabilities than today's fighter jets

[2486] Modernization is therefore about more than just replacing an aging fighter jet with a new one; it is just as much about reviewing the conceptual thinking and the way the Air Force organizes and conducts its operations

[2487] In this way, the decision to acquire the F-35 is the most important driver for the alignment of the air defense of the future

[2488] It is necessary to ensure good coherence between the introduction and localization of new combat aircraft and the localization of the Air Force's other structure

[2489] The Air Force's broad material structure, combined with operations in a wide range of locations in the country, results in a comprehensive and costly organization with regard to materiel, personnel and EBA

[2490] The current base structure is larger than what is needed operationally or in terms of force production

[2491] Through the amendments presented in this proposal, the government has

[2492] Emphasis is placed on continuing and strengthening the operational structure, while taking necessary steps in the base and support structure

[2494] The ability to monitor the airspace over Norway and adjacent areas is an important peacekeeping task that is carried out continuously every day, year-round

[2495] The government has therefore placed emphasis on a basic solution that ensures that this type of task can be carried out at the current level

[2496] A collection of fighter jets at Ørland would make it challenging to meet the need for sovereignty assertion and a fighter aircraft presence in the north

[2497] The government will therefore establish a forward operating base at Evenes, in addition to the main base at Ørland

[2498] A forward operating base is not a two-base solution, but will ensure the presence of combat aircraft

[2551] report is an important part of the government's decision-making basis related to the location of new combat aircraft

[2555] Requirements for future combat air base solution – assessment criteria In order to arrive at a future combat air base solution, extensive analyses and assessments have been carried out within three main areas: operational conditions, the consequences for civilian society and the costs of the various location alternatives

[2556] Operational conditions have been assessed with regard to the suitability of the various alternatives for daily force production and the execution of operations

[2557] The consequences for civil society have been assessed with regard to noise and the environment, consequences for civil aviation, and regional consequences

[2558] The costs for the various alternatives have been calculated and assessed with regard to investment, operation and lifetime costs

[2559] These topics are described in detail in the above-mentioned study report, and a summary description of the most important issues is provided below

[2562] In order for the combat air force to be able to carry out national tasks across the entire conflict spectrum, from daily peacekeeping operations to high-intensity combat operations, it is essential that Box

[2563] Details on the conceptual solution and financial calculations for location alternatives for the Norwegian Armed Forces' new combat aircraft

[2564] The Ministry of Defence has prepared a conceptual solution for a new combat air base structure in accordance with guidelines from the Ministry of Finance

[2565] The study contains a needs analysis, a strategy document that defines the objectives, a requirements document, an opportunities chapter, an alternatives analysis, and treatment of priced consequences in an uncertainty analysis

[2566] The alternatives that have been studied are Bodø, Evenes and Ørland and combinations of these in two-base solutions

[2567] Various options for advanced location of combat aircraft on standby have also been studied

[2568] For all the relevant siting alternatives, a lifetime cost has been calculated over a time horizon of 40 years until 2052, when the F-35 is expected to be phased out

[2569] Lifetime costs consist of investment and operating costs and are expressed as a present value

[2570] Present value calculations are suitable for comparing and ranking alternatives where investment and operating costs are phased in differently over time

[2571] The present value expresses the value of future cash flows, discounted at a discount rate of two percent

[2572] The calculations mainly include receipts and disbursements (cash flows) for personnel, materiel and infrastructure

[2573] The same unit cost growth has been used as in the fighter aircraft program, with a real growth of 2.0 percent per year for personnel and 1.6 percent per year for other cash flows

[2574] Uncertainty premiums are taken into account through separate uncertainty analyses of the input data, where expected values and dispersion measures are calculated for all types of cash flows

[2575] The calculations are supplemented with sensitivity analyses to reveal how robust the cost differences between the alternatives are to changes in, among other things, growth factors, discount rate and the length of the analysis period

[2576] In order to compare the alternatives from a socio-economic perspective, priced costs and revenues that affect actors other than the Armed Forces have been identified and included

[2577] This has generally applied to civil aviation, but a number of non-priced consequences for the rest of society are also described in the conceptual solution

[2578] A defense for our time means that the combat aircraft are located at the airfield that provides the best possible conditions for daily training, while at the same time enabling the maintenance of peacekeeping missions related to asserting sovereignty and presence

[2579] The Air Force's base and support structure must primarily contribute to ensuring that the Armed Forces can carry out its tasks and must therefore be based on the needs associated with operational activities, i.e. force production and operations

[2580] To ensure efficient force production, new combat aircraft will need good access to training areas over land and sea in reasonable proximity to their home bases

[2581] The airport must also have a capacity and regularity that makes it possible to handle the necessary number of aircraft movements in concentrated periods while at the same time meeting the requirement for flight safety

[2582] It is also important that the choice of solution takes into account flexibility and the possibility of further development in a long-term perspective

[2583] The combat aircraft base solution must ensure that the combat aircraft can contribute to task resolution across the entire spectrum of conflicts across Norway and in Norway's areas of interest

[2584] Some of these tasks are carried out continuously every day, year-round, including through fighter aircraft on QRA readiness

[2585] Other tasks, which will be more relevant in connection with a heightened state of readiness, will have to be solved from forward operating bases in the relevant operational area

[2586] The base solution must therefore ensure the ability to quickly establish high military readiness, as well as the ability to quickly react and be present in connection with an incident or crisis management from bases other than the aircraft's home base

[2587] Today's two combat air bases have considerable activity from allied air forces and air forces from several partner countries

[2588] It is in Norway's interest that this activity can be maintained, and if desired also increased, after a new combat air base solution has been established

[2589] The development of military operations shows a trend towards increasingly closer cooperation between air, land and naval forces

[2590] Even smaller operations usually involve elements from at least two branches of defense simultaneously, and the chosen solution should address the need for joint training between combat aircraft and own land and naval forces

[2591] The Air Force is a competence-intensive organization that depends on stability in its personnel

[2592] Preserving the existing professional environments will be crucial for the implementation of the new combat aircraft in the structure, and it is therefore important that the localization does not result in an unacceptable loss of expertise and that it meets the recruitment needs

[2593] The Armed Forces place great emphasis on protecting environmental and natural interests from the stresses that necessary activities entail, and base measures must therefore be assessed based on the negative consequences they may have in relation to noise and the environment, among other things

[2594] The biggest environmental challenge associated with the F-35 is considered to be related to noise, but the consequences for the landscape, natural environment, cultural heritage, cultural environment and reindeer herding have also been assessed

[2595] It is therefore important that the chosen location solution allows the flight activity to be carried out without excessive noise pollution in the surrounding area

[2596] Extensive calculations and assessments have been carried out to compare the consequences of noise for the various location alternatives, and these are documented in a separate study report from Forsvarsbygg

[2597] The study also includes different flight profiles and routes, as well as runway solutions at each airport/base

[2598] The location of new combat aircraft will also have district-level consequences for the municipalities and regions affected

[2599] The government's decision in the case was therefore based on analyses to determine the extent to which settlement and employment are affected by the various location alternatives

[2600] The location of new combat aircraft could have consequences for civil aviation with regard to both ground operations and airspace activity

[2603] Location of new combat aircraft – recommended solution The Government recommends locating the Armed Forces' new combat aircraft at Ørland

[2604] The recommended solution involves closing down Bodø main airport

[2605] Furthermore, it is recommended to establish a forward operating base for combat aircraft with permanent combat aircraft readiness (QRA - Quick Reaction Alert) at Evenes

[2606] Pending the establishment of a new combat air base structure, the air defense structure has had a shared location between Bodø and Ørland

[2607] The government plans to move the remaining part of the air defense at Bodø to a new combat air base at Ørland

[2608] The base defense capacity (base set) at Ørland and Rygge is recommended to be combined at a new combat air base at Ørland, as a flexible resource that can be used both nationally and abroad

[2609] The Government further recommends that force production within air defense and base for- 2011–2012 Prop

[2610] A defence force response, including associated school activities, is being moved to the fighter airbase to create larger, more flexible and robust professional environments

[2611] Station Group Banak is currently subordinate to Bodø Main Air Station

[2612] The closure of Bodø means that the Banak station group will be subordinated to another air station

[2613] Ørland will be further developed as a combat aircraft base with adapted operational and administrative infrastructure so that it is capable of receiving and operating new combat aircraft when they are phased in

[2614] Evenes will be developed with a view to ensuring QRA readiness and the presence of combat aircraft in connection with training and exercises

[2615] The permanent presence at Evenes will be limited to taking care of the QRA mission as well as functions and infrastructure related to preparation for and support of periodic training and exercises

[2616] More about the recommended solution Choosing Ørland as a combat air base involves choosing a base that provides optimal conditions for daily force production while ensuring freedom of action and flexibility for the future

[2617] The location provides the presence of significant military capacity and capability in southern and central Norway, with a short distance to densely populated areas, the capital and oil resources in the North Sea and off Western Norway

[2618] However, a concentration of all combat aircraft at Ørland would entail a reduced capability overall compared to the current solution, particularly with regard to range, reaction time and holding time to operational areas furthest north

[2619] Asserting sovereignty through QRA is a clear expression of Norwegian security policy and allied unity in peacetime, and the government has emphasized in its recommendation the continuation of QRA at its current level

[2620] A forward operating base with QRA in the north provides some of the operational advantages of the two-base solution, while at the same time providing approximately the same operational advantages as a purely singlebase solution, as there will be no need for extensive resources to operate the QRA detachment

[2621] The forward base at Evenes can be quickly reinforced with a significant number of aircraft if deemed necessary, for example in connection with the establishment of high alert military readiness (HLB

[2622] The solution will also be less vulnerable overall with regard to a possible outage at one of the bases

[2623] It is an advantage that the forward operating base is located further north than Bodø, as it will provide better range and endurance in the northernmost operational areas

[2624] Evenes is considered the best location for a forward operating base

[2625] Evenes has a significant and up-to-date military infrastructure that makes the base a good operating base in peacetime, crisis and war, both for fighter jets and other military units

[2626] In an imagined war scenario, Evenes provides great survivability

[2627] Evenes, with its scattered settlements, has little noise impact

[2628] Evenes will also involve relatively small investment costs as most of the infrastructure already exists at the base

[2629] At the same time, the flight operational restrictions at Evenes are not considered to be greater than the ability to maintain flight activity in a satisfactory manner

[2630] Evenes is therefore the most appropriate airport as a forward operating base

[2631] Evenes also has a location that reduces the need for additional deployment bases in the north

[2632] The forward operating base at Evenes will provide short reaction times and short distances to relevant operational areas in the north

[2633] Evenes is also used regularly today in connection with exercises by Norwegian and allied helicopter units, special forces and others, and it is possible to rotate the personnel who will be at the forward operating base in the future

[2634] A concentration of combat aircraft at a main base places great demands on the base's capacity, that is, the ability to carry out the necessary number of aircraft movements

[2635] Orland Main Air Station is a military air station with little civil air traffic, which provides very good conditions for cost-effective and flexible implementation of the necessary number of aircraft movements and other air military activities

[2636] The production of fighter aircraft capacity is mainly concentrated in training areas where fighter aircraft can train with the fewest possible restrictions in the form of altitude limitations or disruption to other air traffic

[2637] A short distance from Ørland, there is good access to airspace for both air-to-air and air-to-ground training

[2638] In the future, it will be important to ensure continued good military airspace access through the development of a satisfactory airspace organization and flexible agreements

[2639] The need for flexibility and freedom of action in a long-term perspective is a very important advantage of a location solution, and as an almost purely military airport, the freedom of action at Ørland is expected to be more real and predictable than at an airport with large civilian operations

[2640] Great freedom of action and flexibility today and in the future is one of the strongest arguments for Ørland as a combat air base

[2641] From a security perspective, the location of Ørland Main Airport and surrounding Prop

[2642] Defense for our contemporary surroundings, in the form of small civilian activities, enables good protection against current threats

[2643] In times of war and crisis, Ørland's secluded location will make offensive operations against the base difficult

[2644] Norway has allied obligations related to future activities at Ørland, as the base is designed for a detachment and deployment of NATO's early warning aircraft (NATO Airborne Early Warning Forward Operating Location – NAEW-FOL

[2646] for the American Marine Corps (Marine Corps Preposition

[2650] The recommended base solution opens up the possibility of establishing and further developing allied training and exercise activities at Ørland, which is desirable from the Norwegian side and very attractive to our allies

[2651] With access to spacious training areas over sea and land near the base, challenging climatic conditions and the possibility of flexible use of multinational network systems, such a solution will ensure both quantitative and qualitative participation from NATO and partner nations

[2654] Fighter aircraft cooperation between Norway, Sweden and Finland can be developed further with Ørland as a fighter aircraft base and Evenes as a forward operating base in the north

[2662] Consequences for civil society

[2663] The recommendation involves the closure of Bodø's main air station and therefore has regional consequences for the Bodø region in the form of a reduction in jobs and population

[2664] Overall, the effects will be significant for both the municipality and the region, but the region as a whole is considered to be able to handle such a reduction in employment and population, especially in light of the fact that other activities in the Air Force have been recommended to be moved to the Bodø region

[2665] A move of current fighter aircraft activity from Bodø to Ørland must be expected to provide Ørland and the surrounding region with a significant population increase and increased employment

[2666] The size of the increase in population and employment will depend on the proportion of immigrants and the proportion who live and work in the region, and who will take advantage of new job opportunities in the Norwegian Defence Forces

[2667] In general, the environmental consequences of having one main base are less than with a split-base solution with fighter aircraft in two locations

[2668] A total of fewer noise-sensitive buildings within the noise zones are expected in a future situation with a main base on Ørland, compared to the current situation with two squadrons in Bodø and one squadron on Ørland

[2671] In addition, measures are expected to be taken on a few buildings in connection with the forward base at Evenes

[2672] Ørland main air station is located close to an important international wetland area (Grandefjæra Nature Reserve), but no physical interventions are expected in this wetland area

[2673] It is nevertheless important that the wetland area is taken into account in the further design of the base

[2674] The Ørland alternative is considered relatively gentle with regard to physical terrain interventions

[2685] Recommended fighter base - summary

[2686] The overall assessment of the alternative bases for the Armed Forces' new combat aircraft indicates that the combat aircraft will be stationed at Ørland and that a forward operating base will be established at Evenes

[2687] Ørland will provide a good basis for combat aircraft capabilities and associated systems such as base support and air defense and, together with the forward base at Evenes, will be a good starting point for operating combat aircraft in southern and northern Norway

[2688] Ørland as a combat air base with large areas and the absence of other actors who could place restrictions on the activity, provides the necessary flexibility and freedom of action with regard to the long-term development of the base and the combat air force

[2689] As a forward operating base, Evenes will ensure the ability to monitor the airspace over Norway and adjacent areas, while the base can be used for periodic combat flight training with our own and allied forces

[2690] A collection of combat aircraft and other parts of the Air Force's other operational activities further provides a basis for developing robust professional environments, as well as safeguarding the personnel and expertise dimension within one geographical area

[2691] Location of new combat aircraft – other considered alternatives

[2692] To arrive at a recommendation for a future combat base solution, in addition to the current two combat air bases Ørland and Bodø, other single-base alternatives, two-base alternatives and forward operating base alternatives have also been considered

[2693] It has not been considered to build a new combat air base in a location without existing military infrastructure or military activities, as this has been considered too costly and would entail an unacceptable risk of loss of expertise

[2694] In addition to the current combat aircraft bases in Bodø and Ørland, the bases at Sola, Rygge, Andøya, Bardufoss, Evenes and Banak have been considered as alternative sole bases for new combat aircraft

[2695] The alternatives Sola, Rygge and Banak are considered irrelevant as sole bases because as sole bases they provide insufficient coverage across the country and very poor coverage in the north (Sola and Rygge) and in the south (Banak), respectively

[2696] Bodø is the base that currently has the bulk of the combat aircraft operations

[2697] Bodø is considered a well-suited starting location for operations throughout the country, and especially in the north

[2698] Bodø is a military airport with extensive civil aviation operations

[2699] The combination of several actors with different interests and needs, as well as limited access to land, creates uncertainty about whether the Bodø alternative provides the Defence with sufficient flexibility and freedom of action in a 30–40 year perspective

[2700] Bodø has more restrictions than Ørland when it comes to access to national training airspace over land and is overall considered a worse alternative than Ørland with regard to force production

[2701] The proximity to the city of Bodø with its large population makes it necessary to move the runway in Bodø due to noise pollution

[2702] Outdoor noise is nevertheless considered to be a major challenge with this solution due to the large number of people affected

[2703] The location near the city of Bodø creates very good conditions with regard to personnel and expertise

[2704] A possible closure of Bodø air station will have negative consequences for employment and settlement in the municipality and the region, but to a relatively lesser extent than if Ørland air station were closed

[2705] Based on the cost analyses that have been carried out, it is considered

[2706] Bodø as a single base solution to be marginally more affordable than the alternatives with regard to operating costs

[2707] A defense for our time approaches in a 40-year perspective

[2708] In terms of investment costs in isolation, Bodø is the most costly single-base solution to establish and it is significantly more expensive than the alternatives

[2709] As a sole base, both Evenes and Bardufoss are considered to have challenges related to flight operational conditions

[2710] The main reason lies in the lack of precision approach systems combined with topographical conditions that make it challenging in terms of safety to conduct combat aircraft operations there every day during the fighter aircraft's lifetime

[2711] Andøya has been rejected as a location due to the consequences of noise

[2712] Noise analyses conducted show that large parts of the center of Andenes fall within the noise zones and that permanent localization of even parts of the combat air force to Andøya means that a new runway solution must be established with associated costs, without necessarily solving the noise challenges satisfactorily

[2713] Various two-base solutions have also been considered

[2714] In order to exploit the advantages of a two-base solution, it is essential that the bases are located with good dispersion between each other and in relation to current areas of operation

[2715] Both with regard to force production and operations, a two-base solution with both bases in the north appears to be impractical

[2716] Both the Bodø–Evenes and Bodø–Andøya combinations are two-base solutions where both bases are located in the north and they are thus not complementary with regard to force production and operations

[2717] A two-base solution should be based on the relevant base in the south, i.e. Ørland, and one of the bases in the north, i.e. Bodø, Evenes, Bardufoss or Andøya

[2718] Of these bases, Bardufoss is considered unsuitable in a two-base solution due to flight operational limitations resulting from inadequate precision approach systems combined with very demanding topography

[2719] Despite challenges related to flight access, Evenes is considered relevant in a two-base solution if Evenes is included with a base that is complementary and that satisfies all flight operational requirements

[2720] Based on this shortlist, the study also assessed the two-base solutions Ørland–Bodø and Ørland–Evenes

[2721] Both of these two-base solutions would be satisfactory, but the fundamental challenge with these two-base solutions is that they are significantly more costly, both in terms of investment and operation, while a regular two-base solution is not operationally required

[2722] From Ørland and northward, the Armed Forces regularly conduct air operational activities at the bases of Bodø, Evenes, Andøya, Bardufoss and Banak

[2723] All of these bases have been considered as alternative forward bases

[2724] In addition to being suitable for carrying out operations, including QRA, the bases must also be acceptable in terms of flight operations and noise for regular combat aircraft activity in connection with training and exercises

[2725] The bases of Bardufoss, Andøya and Evenes are located so close to each other that there is no significant difference between them in terms of the ability to solve the QRA mission related to sovereignty assertion

[2726] All three of these bases, as well as Bodø, will enable QRA mission solutions similar to today and are therefore suitable

[2727] Banak will also be able to solve the QRA mission, but a permanent location of the F-35 so far north and east is not recommended due to needs related to force protection as well as the need for investments in fighter-related infrastructure and noise measures

[2728] For flight operational and flight safety reasons, Bardufoss has also previously been considered unsuitable as a permanent base for combat aircraft

[2729] An extension of the runway, at a significant investment cost, will improve flight operating conditions

[2730] Even with an extensive extension of the runway, the airport will have greater flight safety challenges than other location alternatives

[2731] The combination of large investment costs and flight operational conditions means that Bardufoss is not recommended as a forward operating base

[2732] Evenes is excluded as a sole base due to flight operational limitations related to the lack of precision approaches from the south combined with somewhat demanding topography

[2733] Low activity provides great flexibility with regard to the handling of air traffic

[2734] These limitations therefore do not prevent Evenes from being a base for QRA and forward operations

[2735] When it comes to noise, including the need for and costs associated with redemption and noise measures on homes, separate noise calculations have been made to assess the suitability and consequences of the various alternatives

[2736] The analyses show that the need for noise measures and associated costs is significantly greater on Andøya and Bodø than on Evenes and Bardufoss

[2737] Evenes is the alternative that results in the fewest people exposed to noise due to small and scattered settlements

[2738] The alternative Bodø with the current runway solution and Andøya with the use of both the main runway and crosswind runway are not considered realistic alternatives either with regard to investment. 2011–

[2739] A defense for our time ring or with regard to what is considered socially acceptable noise consequences

[2740] In terms of operation, Andøya and Bardufoss are considered to be cheaper to operate than Evenes and Bodø

[2741] This is because these two bases currently have military operations, which will provide synergy effects that can be exploited in the form of lower operating costs

[2742] Bodø will be on a par with Evenes, as it is assumed that Bodø's main air station will be closed if Ørland is chosen as the main base

[2743] Specifically, this means that the support organizations that need to be established at Bardufoss and Andøya will be somewhat less personnel-intensive than what is correspondingly necessary at Evenes and Bodø

[2744] Evenes will also involve relatively low investment costs as most of the infrastructure already exists at the base

[2745] At the same time, the flight operational limitations at Evenes are not considered to be greater than the ability to maintain flight activity in a satisfactory manner

[2746] Overall, Evenes is considered the most appropriate airport for a forward operating base

[2747] Conclusion – location of fighter aircraft

[2748] It is recommended that Bodø main airport be closed

[2749] The Norwegian Armed Forces' new fighter aircraft, air defense and base defense are recommended to be gathered within a newly established Ørland Air Station as a single base

[2750] Furthermore, the establishment of a forward operating base for combat aircraft with permanent combat readiness (QRA) at Evenes is recommended

[2751] The permanent presence will be limited to the maintenance of the QRA mission as well as a minimum of functions and infrastructure related to preparation for and support of periodic training and exercises

[2752] Future need for analysis capacity

[2753] Location of the Armed Forces' EK Support Center New combat aircraft provides a significantly greater amount of collected data compared to previous combat aircraft systems

[2754] This requires greater resources for analysis

[2755] The Norwegian Air Force currently has a dispersed analysis environment, linked to the various aircraft systems

[2756] The Norwegian Defence Forces' EK Support Centre (FEKS) located at Rygge maintains national expertise in exploiting the electromagnetic spectrum by using already collected information to implement active and passive measures

[2757] FEKS supports the entire Armed Forces, including updating important systems that strengthen survivability in operations

[2758] The development of the Air Force's capabilities provides an ever-increasing ability to collect information through new and better sensors

[2759] The Air Force's organization must be adapted to the increasing need to be able to analyze, process and distribute the information that is collected, so that the potential of the sensors can be better utilized to create operational effect

[2760] There is a need for a more centralized and interdisciplinary organization to handle such tasks in the future

[2761] New combat aircraft will also require capacity in the groundbased organization to be able to utilize the capabilities of the aircraft effectively and to handle information processing

[2762] FEKS is recommended to be located in Ørland as part of the necessary development of the Air Force's organization, where the combat aircraft environment and the technology surrounding it are central

[2763] The role as a support and competence center for the entire Armed Forces EK environment will be continued

[2764] Further development of the analysis capacity will be considered in light of the phasing in of the F-35 and new air command and control solution

[2766] Economic consequences of the recommended solution

[2767] The transition from today's F-16 located at Bodø and Ørland to the F-35 at Ørland with a forward operating base at Evenes, based on the overall ambition, involves an estimated total investment in the base structure of approximately kr 5.1 billion for the Armed Forces

[2768] The new fighter base structure is estimated to have a positive operating effect of approximately NOK 70 million per year compared to the current solution with F-16s located in Ørland and Bodø

[2769] Operating new fighter aircraft from Ørland as a fighter base is estimated to result in increased annual operating costs of approximately NOK 300 million, once the new fighter aircraft have been fully phased in

[2770] Including the advanced QRA base at Evenes, the total increased annual operating cost will be approximately NOK 375 million compared to the current operation of F-16s

[2832] The Army, the Navy, the Home Guard and joint capabilities

[2833] This chapter describes other parts of the Armed Forces with an emphasis on development and proposed changes

[3349] Other agencies, state enterprises and other policy areas

[3350] This chapter deals with the defense sector's agencies and state enterprises other than the Armed Forces

[3351] In addition, research policy and regional policy issues are discussed

[3352] National Security Authority The National Security Authority (NSM) was established on 1 January 2003 as a civilian directorate for preventive security services. The NSM is to be a driving force for improving the security situation and provide advice on the development of security work in society

[3353] NSM shall facilitate, support and report on the implementation of defensive preventive measures against espionage, sabotage and terrorist acts in all sectors

[3354] This is done by supervising and exercising authority, notifying and handling serious computer attacks, developing security measures and providing advice and guidance within preventive security

[3355] In this context, preventive security refers to defensive measures to protect information, information systems and other objects against espionage, sabotage and terror

[3356] The measures include measures to create robust barriers, and the ability to detect security-threatening incidents and vulnerabilities, adequately respond and restore a secure state

[3357] These measures are primarily implemented within the businesses themselves

[3358] NSM will create the best possible conditions for this to happen in a targeted, cost-effective and minimally invasive manner for the individual

[3359] One of the main tasks of the NSM is to exercise the function as a national security authority in accordance with the Act on Preventive Security Services (the Security Act

[3360] The function of the national security authority involves coordinating preventive security measures, monitoring the security situation in the businesses to which the Security Act applies, and acting as an executive body in cooperation with other countries and international organizations

[3361] Furthermore, the function involves obtaining and assessing information of importance for the implementation of preventive security services, supervising the security situation in the businesses, contributing to the development of security measures, and providing information, advice and guidance to the businesses

[3362] In addition to its function as a national security authority, NSM, as a directorate, also handles a number of other tasks within security

[3363] This includes, among other things, the task as a national alert and handling body for serious attacks against socially critical ICT infrastructure (NorCERT), the role as a certification authority for IT security in products and systems (CERTIT), certain control tasks in accordance with the Defence Secrets Act and the Defence-Important Inventions Act, as well as the secretariat function for the Coordination Committee for Preventive Information Security (KIS

[3364] NSM is administratively subordinate to and reports to the Ministry of Defence for task performance in the defence sector and reports to the Ministry of Justice and Public Security for the civilian sector

[3365] A challenging security situation

[3366] The dependence on ICT and the internet is today a strategic security challenge

[3367] Both the Armed Forces, civilian authorities and large Norwegian companies with critical societal functions depend on ICT to deliver their services

[3368] We live in a network-based society where sectors are interdependent on each other and on functioning computer networks

[3369] The addiction also crosses national borders

[3370] With increasing interdependence between different critical components of society, multiple critical targets or functions can be intentionally or unintentionally damaged or crippled in a single attack

[3371] Technological developments present significant challenges in terms of ensuring sufficient security of ICT systems against serious incidents

[3372] The threat from actors who use ICT as a tool is large and increasing, in addition to the methods used becoming more advanced and targeted

[3373] CERT has experienced a tripling in the number of ICT incidents over the past four years

[3374] In 2011, NorCERT handled over 20 serious incidents, and it is believed that there are large underreporting figures

[3375] At the same time as the threat is increasing, NSM has recently uncovered a number of specific shortcomings in preventive security

[3376] A defense of our time's work

[3377] The gap between threats and security measures is widening

[3378] This means that the security situation is deteriorating

[3379] Need for a holistic approach

[3380] The societal benefits and value of well-functioning ICT systems are great

[3381] In a networked society, everyone is mutually dependent on the same infrastructure, technology and the same systems

[3382] The use of new computer systems, industrial and process control systems, mobile phones, flash drives, social media and e-readers has made us more vulnerable to data breaches and attacks

[3383] The ever-increasing number of threats related to the information society has highlighted the need for a more holistic approach to the challenges, across the various sectors

[3384] NSM has special authority in relation to the processing of classified information, which is clearly regulated in the Security Act

[3385] The businesses regulated by the Security Act also process large amounts of internal and sensitive information that falls outside this legislation and is not regulated to the same extent

[3386] Holistic governance, responsibility and roles are essential to tackling new challenges within information security

[3387] There is therefore a need to strengthen expertise in information security

[3388] This applies to both expertise in vulnerabilities and threats, as well as expertise in security challenges

[3389] The project “Evaluation and further development of the National Security Authority” will assess the need for a more holistic approach to the various security challenges based on what society as a whole needs across current sectoral thinking

[3390] NSM can be a tool for achieving the goals of more holistic management and organization of security work

[3391] It is planned that research and development activities at NSM will be continued

[3392] Strengthening NorCERT

[3393] The Norwegian Computer Emergency Response Team (NorCERT) is part of NSM and contributes through ongoing operational activities with effective measures against internet threats and attacks against public and private enterprises with important societal functions

[3394] The Digital Infrastructure Alert System is part of NorCERT, and provides the authorities with the ability to alert and verify serious and coordinated attacks against socially important ICT infrastructure

[3395] It is planned to strengthen NorCERT to enable Norwegian businesses to face increased threats and vulnerabilities and to detect and handle serious computer attacks, as well as increase NorCERT’s ability to notify an increasing number of Norwegian businesses that have been affected or are at risk of being affected by computer attacks

[3396] The development of response environments for ICT incidents, which is now happening in several sectors, requires NorCERT to be able to respond to incidents when they occur

[3397] It is important that Norwegian businesses receive increased assistance in analyzing equipment that may be compromised, so that more espionage attacks and intelligence over computer networks in businesses are detected

[3398] Norway will thus be better able to meet and deal with the increased threats to computer networks

[3399] Increased emphasis on preventive safety

[3647] Competence and personnel

[3648] One of the defense sector's most important strategic challenges is the ability to attract, recruit, develop, employ and retain the right personnel with the right expertise

[3649] The concept of competence is used to describe the knowledge, insight, experience, characteristics, skills and attitudes required to solve a task

[3650] The tasks and organization of the Armed Forces have changed significantly since the current personnel and competence structures were established

[3651] The defense sector and its employees have been through a series of restructurings that have changed the Defense Forces' tasks, materiel, and location structure

[3652] From being an invasion defense mainly based on mobilization, where the peace structure produced expertise for a planned war structure, the Armed Forces today produce and use expertise to solve a broad spectrum of continuous tasks nationally and internationally

[3653] The same departments and personnel should be able to complete assignments at home as well as abroad

[3654] There have been a number of measures in the area of personnel and expertise, but the area as a whole has not been transformed after the transition to a response defense

[3655] Society at large has also changed

[3656] Norway is today a high-tech knowledge society

[3657] The pace of change and technological development has been particularly high in the military sector

[3658] A modern network-based emergency defense system has high system complexity with several unique systems that place high demands on the operators' expertise and on continuity in many functions

[3659] At the same time, the high rate of change requires employees who are adaptable, and a network-based response defense requires greater cognitive and competence diversity among employees

[3660] The armed forces must be able to attract other groups and categories in society than before and recruit employees with different educational and experience backgrounds

[3661] Changing assignments may require new types of expertise

[3662] The defense sector's existing expertise must also be developed and applied in different ways than today

[3663] An increasing focus on attitudes, ethics and leadership within all areas of business also affects the requirements for competence in the defense sector

[3664] Increased globalization and internationalization provide new opportunities for expanded cooperation with other nations

[3665] A more integrated, multinational collaboration can contribute to effective solutions, also within the area of expertise and personnel

[3666] Demographic and societal trends, together with the defense sector's own development, will greatly influence the sector's ability to recruit, develop and retain expertise

[3667] The labor market is more globalized than before and is characterized by a higher degree of mobility both domestically and across national borders

[3668] The Armed Forces are currently in fewer places than before, daily contact with the population is less than before, while the volume of first-time service has been adapted to the Armed Forces' needs and reduced

[3669] Today, both men and women are working

[3670] Career decisions must take into account the overall needs of the family

[3671] This affects, among other things, relocation, commuter schemes, local business and employment, and long-term perspective and predictability in career planning

[3672] Certain parts of the organization, and certain types of expertise, currently bear a large part of the burden in relation to international assignments

[3673] International operations also place significant pressure on the families of many defense personnel, and there is a certain excess frequency of breakups compared to the normal population

[3674] Today's labor market involves great competition for labor, and a number of categories of expertise in the Armed Forces are highly sought after in the civilian labor market

[3675] This applies in particular to technical competence, and is a challenge in the Navy, the Air Force and the Armed Forces' logistics organization, among other things

[3676] In many categories, such as medical health personnel, it is challenging for the Armed Forces to recruit expertise from the civilian sector

[3677] These challenges place changed and new demands on the defense sector as an employer

[3678] Without good strategic competence management, there is a risk, for example, that the benefits of large material procurements cannot be realized because the Armed Forces do not have the necessary competence

[3679] A defense for our time

[3680] In Norway, women's labor force participation is very high, and this has been one of the most important prerequisites for growth and prosperity in Norwegian society

[3681] It is a significant challenge for the sector to attract, recruit and retain employees who differ from the majority in the organization

[3682] This applies particularly to the female part of the population

[3683] The sector does not sufficiently recruit talent from the full breadth of society

[3684] It can have procedural, structural, reputational as well as organizational cultural reasons

[3685] In the operational defense, there is a need for a qualitative approach to competence, rather than the invasion defence's quantitative understanding of the concept of personnel

[3686] The personnel and competence area has not been the subject of a comprehensive and systematic review to adapt the Armed Forces to the fundamental organizational and societal changes that have taken place in recent decades

[3687] Overall objectives The main objective of the defence sector's personnel policy is to strengthen the work of recruiting, retaining and further developing both military and civilian employees with high motivation and the right skills, adapted to the needs and tasks of the Armed Forces

[3688] The objectives that apply to the personnel and competence area were formulated in the St.prop

[3689] No. 48 (2007–

[3690] These are being continued with further development in some key areas

[3691] The Government's main priorities for the personnel and competence area in this long-term plan are as follows

[3692] – The government will address the defense sector's competence challenges as a strategic development theme

[3693] The sector shall be a modern competence organization and continue its development from more traditional personnel management to strategic management of personnel development

[3694] Competence management should be an integrated part of strategic management in the sector, and personnel allocations should ensure good utilization of competence and build on the organization's learning

[3695] Broader recruitment, a two-way flow of skills with society at large, and more flexible career paths will meet the sector's needs for both broad and specialized expertise. – The operational requirements and needs govern the personnel and expertise structure

[3696] The ability to conduct operations is the core of the military profession

[3697] The main focus for competence building in the Armed Forces must therefore be based on broad and comprehensive knowledge of military operations and relevant technology and subject areas

[3698] At the same time, it is important that the Armed Forces, in areas beyond military expertise, recruit personnel with expertise from society at large to a greater extent than today and integrate them into the expertise organization. – The defense sector should be an attractive and safe workplace that safeguards employees and their opportunity to have the most normal family life possible

[3699] This includes the care of personnel before, during and after international operations

[3700] The Government will further develop the work to strengthen recognition and care for veterans in line with the Government's action plan "In Service of Norway

[3701] – The defense sector should recruit employees who represent greater diversity in background, characteristics, skills and experience, in order to better meet the varied tasks that a modern operational defense must solve

[3702] Greater diversity is also important for the sector to reflect society and utilize society's overall expertise resources

[3703] Not least, it is important to ensure that the sector is an attractive workplace for women as well

[3704] – The foundation of the Armed Forces is, and will continue to be, conscription

[3705] Military defense is a fundamental task that citizens should stand together for

[3706] Conscription is intended to contribute to the Defence's anchoring and legitimacy in society by ensuring a broad recruitment base that reflects the population

[3707] The first-aid service will be further developed and adapted to the operational defence's requirements for responsiveness, operational departments' need for flexibility and freedom of action, as well as increased requirements for competence and cost-effectiveness

[3708] – The defense sector is in a mutually dependent relationship with society at large

[3709] The defense sector should reflect societal developments to the greatest extent possible and contribute to them, for example through family and life-stage policies, inclusive working life and diversity

[3710] The response sector must, to a greater extent, see its own competence needs and its own competence production as part of society's overall resources, to a greater extent than today, use competence developed outside the sector and collaborate with the civilian education system

[3711] Increased globalization, internationalization and multinational force contributions provide new opportunities for expanded cooperation with other countries, also in the area of personnel and expertise

[3712] A defense for our time

[3713] Skills reform The defense sector's ability to attract, develop and manage skills will be a key issue in the years to come

[3714] The restructuring of the Armed Forces after the Cold War has led to a series of extensive changes for employees

[3715] In contrast, the personnel and competence area as a whole has not been an integrated part of the transition to a dedicated defence force

[3716] The continued modernization of the Norwegian Armed Forces will not succeed if it primarily concerns structure, geography and materiel procurement, but omits the area of personnel and expertise

[3717] Equipment investments can only be converted into operational capability if the Armed Forces have people who can operate the equipment

[3718] The personnel and competence area has to a limited extent been the subject of a comprehensive and systematic analysis and development of measures across the sector in the transition from a mobilization to a response defense

[3719] It will therefore be a main priority for the Government to address personnel and competence as a long-term strategic development issue

[3720] Among the key issues and challenges, there are five areas in particular that will be in focus during the further work

[3721] Competence organization and strategic competence management Personnel and competence have been seen too largely as an area of managerial and administrative nature, and not as an integrated part of strategic business management

[3722] The defense sector must be a modern competence organization, and strategic competence management must be an integrated part of leadership and management in the defense sector's agencies

[3723] Investments in competence must be recognized as a crucial factor in the realization of material investments and the development of operational capability

[3724] The defense sector's missions and tasks are becoming increasingly complex and place increasingly higher demands on competence, which reinforces the need for strategic competence management

[3725] Better systems must be established to ensure that the competence acquired by individual employees remains in the organization, by retaining the right personnel, and through better systems for sharing and documenting experiences and knowledge

[3726] Develop and apply your skills

[3727] The defense sector must develop and apply expertise in a better and more systematic way to meet future expertise needs

[3728] Competence development must be guided to a greater extent by the organisation's strategic assessments and needs

[3729] Through broader recruitment and flexible career paths, the sector must ensure a diversity of expertise that takes care of the need for continuity, quality and flexibility, and for broad as well as specialized expertise

[3730] Needs-oriented structures, systems and processes

[3731] The defense sector must have needs-oriented structures, which, together with simplified systems and processes, facilitate attracting, recruiting, developing, utilizing and retaining the expertise the agencies need

[3732] The Armed Forces have a far greater need than before for cutting-edge expertise, and this requires systems that facilitate a career as a specialist

[3733] The salary system should also reflect the actual additional burden that various tasks and activities in today's emergency defense impose on employees

[3734] In this context, it may be appropriate, in consultation with the employee organizations, to assess the relationship between the personnel's fixed salary and bonuses within the framework of a continued total salary volume

[3735] As a result of the competence reform, and as an integrated part of it, there will also be a need for a comprehensive review of the command system to ensure that it is adapted to the needs of the operational defence forces and their employees, and to the development of society

[3736] The interdependence between the various elements of the business is crucial to providing operational capability – everyone in the value chain contributes in an interaction to achieve common goals

[3737] The defense sector's deliveries depend on quality in all pillars of expertise and a recognition of the interdependence between the various areas of expertise and functions

[3738] Strategic management of the personnel and competence area must be an integrated part of management and governance in the sector

[3739] This requires high-quality processes, the production of sufficient fact-based basic material, and the use of this in decision-making

[3740] Active ownership of developments in the personnel area beyond structure and material must be a central part of the managers' task, and a culture must be developed so that managers are also measured on the achievement of results in this area

[3741] Furthermore, the organizational culture must reflect the 2011–

[3742] A defense for our time political goals in the area of ​​personnel and competence

[3743] Leaders are important carriers of culture, and therefore have a special responsibility to ensure this

[3744] Interaction with society at large

[3745] The defense sector is in a mutually dependent relationship with society at large

[3746] Demographic trends, such as urbanization, increased worker mobility and a social structure that is increasingly based on dual-career families, place new demands on the defense sector as an employer

[3747] These must be met in close collaboration with society at large

[3748] Furthermore, the defense sector must reflect the society of which it is a part to the greatest extent possible, including through greater diversity among employees

[3749] The Armed Forces have had a tradition of producing expertise for society, but have to a limited extent used expertise developed by others

[3750] There must therefore be greater provision for a two-way flow of expertise between the sector and the rest of society

[3751] The Armed Forces have had internal systems and mechanisms for generating the necessary expertise, and to a limited extent have used society's overall research and educational resources or considered their own educational capacity as part of these

[3752] In order to exploit synergies in society and ensure the sector has a better source of knowledge and expertise, opportunities for collaboration in education, research and development with civilian research and educational environments must be exploited

[3753] The ability to solve important and demanding societal tasks requires better utilization of society's overall resources, for example through increased cross-sectoral cooperation

[3754] In this context, it is also important that the Armed Forces recruit broadly in the future to meet its competence needs, and to a greater extent than today, use competence from the civilian sector where it is natural

[3755] Further process

[3756] The government has initiated strategic work to address the sector's competence challenges, where challenges and solutions must be seen in a holistic context

[3757] The work will be based on the areas outlined above, as well as a more thorough mapping of the personnel and expertise structure within each agency and how these support the goals of the agencies and the sector

[3758] This will form the basis for distinguishing between areas where measures can be taken in the short term and areas that require further investigation and analysis

[3759] The government will continue the good dialogue with employee organizations as a central part of the work on the reform

[3760] The government aims to return to the Storting with a report on this work by the end of the year

[3761] Further development of current policy

[3762] The objectives for the personnel and competence area as formulated in the St.prop

[3763] No. 48 (2007–2008) is fixed

[3764] The Government nevertheless sees a need to further develop certain important areas or make adjustments within them

[3765] Initial service

[3766] General conscription today means that all men who are found capable of military service are subject to conscription

[3767] The essence of conscription is that all able-bodied Norwegian male citizens shall be at the disposal of the nation from the age of 18 to 44, i.e. a total of 25 years

[3768] Military service is not the same as initial service

[3769] Eligible persons who are not called up for service in the first instance are still subject to military service and can be called up if the need arises

[3770] In other words, conscripts perform their duty even if they are not called up and complete their initial service

[3771] General conscription is thus a national emergency plan, in case there should be times when the population must be mobilized to protect our country

[3772] The foundation of the Armed Forces is and will continue to be conscription

[3773] General conscription means that all able-bodied Norwegian male citizens must take their share of the responsibility that military defense entails, and be at the disposal of the nation from the age of 18 to

[3774] Conscription contributes, among other things, to ensuring the legitimacy of the Armed Forces and their anchoring in society through broad recruitment to the Armed Forces that reflects the population

[3775] The practice of military service through initial service must ensure this function

[3776] Conscription has broad support in Norway

[3777] According to Folk og Forsvar's annual opinion poll, 75 percent responded in 2011 that they want to Prop

[3778] A defense for our time maintained conscription, while 20 percent were against it

[3779] Conscription is central to ensuring that the Armed Forces have a broad recruitment of suitable personnel across social and cultural divides, while at the same time ensuring that important peacekeeping tasks are carried out

[3780] Conscripts entering their first term of service perform a number of ongoing peacetime tasks

[3781] For example, conscripts man the Guard and Border Guard, the Navy's vessels and the Air Force's bases

[3782] The soldiers are also trained to cover parts of the brigade's strength needs and form the basis for parts of the army reserve

[3783] Initial service also forms an important recruitment basis for, among other things, enlistment, basic officer training, service in international operations and for staffing the Home Guard structure

[3784] Conscripts who have completed their initial service are also an important resource for society and the Armed Forces after completing their service

[3785] A large proportion of crews are deployed in the Home Guard, and are also an important source of recruitment for international operations

[3786] Furthermore, people who have completed their first-time service are an important resource for society from a societal security perspective

[3787] The initial service will continue to contribute to ensuring operational capability and the ability to build up forces in line with the Armed Forces' planning

[3788] However, the current conscription model has some weaknesses, and the main point of complaint is that initial service is still largely designed to produce endurance rather than responsiveness, and therefore the Armed Forces provide too few forces with high responsiveness

[3789] The first-time service must therefore be further developed and adapted to the needs of the operational defense

[3790] The government believes that the conscription model must take into account increased demands for quality, greater complexity, reuse of personnel and cost-effectiveness

[3791] This will therefore open up the possibility of a greater degree of differentiation of initial service in the Army

[3792] The Navy and Air Force will further develop the current 12-month service within the current framework

[3793] Today's youth are growing up in a society with a much faster rate of technological change than previous generations, and are therefore better prepared to meet many of the demands of a modern and high-tech defense

[3794] Recruitment and selection must be adapted to the actual needs for competence and cognitive skills among personnel that a network-based response defense entails

[3795] Although traditional requirements specifications with a primary emphasis on physical capacity will still be relevant for some functions, the needs of today's and future defense mean that emphasis must also be placed on other characteristics and skills

[3796] The function of conscription in terms of anchoring and legitimizing the Armed Forces among the people and ensuring the Armed Forces' opportunities to recruit from among the most suitable people in society can only be partially fulfilled as long as conscription only covers the male part of the population

[3797] It is therefore a weakness of the current system that it is different for women and men

[3798] Conscription does not reflect the actual need for manpower and expertise in today's defense

[3799] Although women's participation in the workforce is very high, Norway has a relatively gender-segregated labor market where the Armed Forces have traditionally not been a typical career choice for women

[3800] The fact that conscription is reserved for men reinforces this tendency and can give an unfortunate and misleading signal about who the Armed Forces want to recruit

[3801] It may also create the unfortunate impression that working in the Armed Forces is best suited for men

[3802] Research suggests that the different framework conditions for women and men in their first-time service negatively affect the climate between them during their service

[3803] In Folk og Forsvar's annual opinion poll, 64 percent in total, and 70 percent of the age group under 30, responded that conscription should apply to both sexes

[3804] A total of 31 percent were against conscription for both sexes, and 28 percent in the age group under

[3805] It is a fundamental value in Norwegian society that rights and obligations are independent of gender

[3806] From a rights and obligations perspective, as well as the Armed Forces' actual competence needs, a gender neutral conscription system should be assessed, based, among other things, on the experiences currently being gained in connection with conscription for women

[3807] Society has a clear responsibility to look after personnel and their loved ones when the Armed Forces participate in international operations

[3809] Personnel in international operations are in service on behalf of the Norwegian state

[3842] Organizations and businesses in the private and public sectors are placing increased emphasis on the connection between diversity and problem solving, and on the fact that a broader range of expertise provides better problem solving

[3843] This connection is not least important for the defense sector, where the tasks to be solved are becoming increasingly varied

[3844] Diversity in an organization is created, among other things, through variation in professional background and expertise, age distribution, variation in ethnic and religious affiliation and sexual orientation, differences in social and geographical background, and a good gender composition

[3845] The goal of increased diversity in the defense sector has several justifications

[3846] Firstly, a working life where everyone can participate, and where women participate on an equal footing with men, is a goal for the government

[3847] It is also a prerequisite for optimal use of society's total workforce and expertise

[3848] Working life should be inclusive and utilize the potential of the staff

[3849] Women's participation in working life is a crucial factor for the success of the Nordic welfare model because it provides better utilization of resources

[3850] A defense for our time, talent acquisition, better utilization of the workforce, and better adaptability

[3851] Women's expertise is a major untapped resource for the Armed Forces

[3852] Secondly, a network-based, high-tech counter-insurgency defense requires different types of expertise than a mobilization-based invasion defense

[3853] In some of the missions the Armed Forces will be carrying out, there will still be a need for employees with very good physical skills, but in more and more positions, it will be more crucial to have, for example, a system and overall understanding, communication skills and simultaneous capacity

[3854] The military's tasks have become more knowledge- and competence-intensive, and require cognitive diversity that ensures that a problem is examined from multiple perspectives

[3855] The drafts are also more varied than before, and it is therefore far more important to ensure that the people recruited to the Armed Forces represent a breadth of skills, characteristics, experience and educational background

[3856] For example, a personnel corps consisting of both women and men, as well as personnel with different backgrounds and experience, can be important for meeting different security needs in operational areas, which is also emphasized in UN Security Resolution

[3857] Thirdly, diversity among employees contributes to increasing the legitimacy of the Armed Forces in society since legitimacy is, among other things, linked to representation and identification with the Armed Forces

[3858] Representation from different groups of the population in the armed forces is therefore a goal in itself, in line with equality and democratic principles

[3859] Greater diversity can have a self-reinforcing effect, as different groups can find role models and identify with the Armed Forces

[3860] A defense without sufficient representation from different groups risks being perceived as less credible, relevant or legitimate

[3861] This can result in lower defensiveness and a weaker reputation

[3862] The defense sector has not been successful enough in its goal of recruiting based on the entire population

[3863] The skills reform will have to look at whether there are aspects of the way the sector attracts and recruits employees that prevent the desired diversity from being achieved

[3864] A main challenge lies in retaining employees with backgrounds different from the majority in organizations, and it is therefore necessary to look at how employees experience being looked after during their service

[3865] The Armed Forces must accept inequality and have zero tolerance for harassment or discrimination based on, for example, gender, sexual orientation or ethnicity

[3866] For greater breadth in recruitment to be of value to the organization, diversity must also be valued and safeguarded

[3867] If the internal socialization processes in the Armed Forces contribute too much to grinding away individual characteristics, the value of cognitive diversity is not being exploited

[3868] Department Commander

[3869] is, in addition to providing the Armed Forces with specialized expertise, experience and continuity at lower levels in the organization, a key instrument for creating a better and more sustainable balance in the age structure in the Armed Forces

[3870] Evaluations of the scheme conclude that random attrition and a low average age among department commanders are a challenge, and that this may mean that the Armed Forces' need for specialized expertise is not being met to a sufficient extent

[3871] The average department commander leaves the Armed Forces at the age of 26 to 27, which is far earlier than the scheme envisaged

[3872] The evaluations further conclude that there are challenges related to employment conditions such as age limit, salary and bonus, skills development and career plans, and visibility and recognition

[3873] Career and competence development must be linked and given importance throughout a department commander's career

[3874] This means continued emphasis on education, other skills development and bonus use

[3875] At the same time, the department commander must be qualified for another career after the end of his employment relationship

[3876] In order to provide the Armed Forces with specialized expertise, experience and continuity, the professional appointment of department commanders according to the Armed Forces' needs shall be continued with minor adjustments to the selection system and the timing of professional appointment than today

[3877] The current selection system involves too homogeneous recruitment and the Armed Forces are not sufficiently achieving the goal of the department commander providing a variety of expertise

[3878] To increase predictability for the department commander, career and service plans should be established that are adapted to a horizontal career

[3879] The Armed Forces must facilitate a more flexible use of time limits in positions to reduce unnecessary rotation in functions where there is a great need for continuity

[3880] The practice of the remuneration system has overly rewarded vertical careers and the development of broad competence, while horizontal careers and increased standing time do not have sufficient incentives

[3881] The salary framework must be used in a way that stimulates longer tenure in a horizontal career path where this is desirable

[3882] A defense for our time

[3883] The increased complexity of the task portfolio of the Norwegian Armed Forces results in a greater need for technical and other specialized expertise and for continuity in specialist functions

[3884] This is particularly a challenge in the Army

[3885] Here, a sustainable concept must be developed for safeguarding specialist expertise and for facilitating career paths that ensure the needs of both the department commander and the Armed Forces in a good way

[3886] The Armed Forces' changing needs for expertise in various categories, as well as developments in the labor market, indicate that there is a greater need to facilitate career change

[3887] The career transition system shall apply to all officers, enlisted personnel and civilians, and ensure a dignified and smooth transition to another activity upon completion of service or contract in the Armed Forces – when this is desired or as a result of redundancy

[3888] For enlisted personnel and department commanders, the career change may also involve a transition to a civilian career in the defense sector or a further military career through professional employment in the Armed Forces

[3889] To qualify for career change, the educational offer for enlisted personnel and department commanders in the Armed Forces should be of civilian merit, either in the form of academic courses (credits) or practically oriented qualifications such as a vocational diploma or certificate

[3890] The Armed Forces' career exchange schemes should be directed towards internal civilian positions, other state or private actors

[3891] In addition to being a good way to safeguard the current personnel, career rotation can help create good personnel dynamics, a good reputation externally, and be a stable source of qualified personnel and expertise for other parts of the sector and for re-recruitment to the Armed Forces

[3917] Part III Implementation and future developments 2011–

[3918] Targeted implementation

[3919] Norway's defense is in a unique situation compared to the defense organizations in many other European countries

[3920] Long-term and sufficiently strict governance, combined with good management of petroleum revenues, gives Norway a freedom of action that few of our European partners have

[3921] Order in the economy is a prerequisite for further developing a strong and modern defense

[3922] In addition, the government has worked purposefully for several years to achieve a sustainable balance between resources, tasks, level of ambition and operational capability

[3923] Today, we have a well-balanced defense, with the ability to carry out today's tasks and at the same time invest in modern and future-oriented capabilities

[3924] The central objective of the current long-term plan was to facilitate such sustainable development of the defense sector, by continuing and further developing the results achieved since

[3925] By the end of 2012, the transformation of the Armed Forces into a modern, flexible and robust defence force with a structure adapted to the security policy challenges of our time will have been largely completed

[3926] This has provided a good foundation for balanced and sustainable development

[3927] Successful implementation of the latest long-term plans, and in particular the long-term plan 2009–2012, has thus provided a good starting point for the further development of the defence sector

[3928] The Government emphasizes that the further development of the defense sector should take place in a holistic manner based on a long-term perspective in which a sustainable balance is maintained

[3929] In line with current security policy challenges, and in order to meet a changing world, the defense sector must be continuously renewed and improved

[3930] This is essential for the defense sector to continue to be a relevant security policy instrument for Norway

[3931] With the security policy basis, the societal and technological developments and the defense policy goals that have been explained in previous chapters, and through the entirety of the measures that follow from this proposition, a solid foundation is established for continued targeted and long-term development of the defense sector

[3932] This is a goal that places high demands on implementation and execution

[3933] The government emphasizes that the further development of the defense sector is based on long-term sustainability

[3934] This includes the acquisition, phasing in and operation of new materiel systems, including new combat aircraft

[3935] Timely implementation of all structural measures and continuous efforts to ensure the most efficient use of the sector's overall resources within specified financial limits are crucial in this context

[3936] The defense sector manages significant resources on behalf of society

[3937] The government sets strict requirements for these resources to be managed effectively and in line with political decisions

[3938] In order to maintain public confidence and achieve the set goals, it is crucial that the defense sector has effective financial management, sound administration and good competence management
