[4316] A defense for our time. The development of the defense in the long term

[4317] This chapter will outline the long-term development of the Armed Forces

[4318] The Armed Forces' material investments and production of military expertise require a planning horizon that extends several decades into the future

[4319] The Government places great emphasis on long-term goals guiding the development of the defense sector

[4320] Long-termism is not just about identifying issues that need to be addressed at a later date

[4321] A long-term perspective must also guide decisions to be made now or in the near future

[4322] Tomorrow's defense is created by today's decisions

[4323] A modern defense cannot be improvised

[4324] If a serious security policy challenge were to arise, it is the planning in the years before that determines what kind of capabilities the Armed Forces have at their disposal

[4325] The developments described in chapters 3 and 4 emphasize the need for a defense that can meet a broad spectrum of possible security challenges and that has the flexibility to adapt to changes in the environment

[4326] Particularly important is the Norwegian Defence Force's ability to prevent conflict and war by constituting a credible military threshold

[4327] The chapter focuses in particular on the long-term development of the Armed Forces' capabilities and operational capability

[4328] There are also a number of long-term challenges in the area of personnel and competence, but this is not addressed in any detail here, as it will be highlighted in the announced parliamentary report on competence

[4330] Stability and uncertainty – the long lines

[4331] Long-term planning is about dealing constructively and rationally with an uncertain future

[4332] Planning must be based on the recognition that the future cannot be predicted

[4333] Experience shows that changes constantly occur that place new demands on the Armed Forces

[4334] The outbreak of civil war-like conflicts towards the end of the 20th century, the serious terrorist attacks in the first decade of the 21st century and the recent development of the threat landscape in digital space are examples of this

[4335] Since the development of military capabilities takes a long time, it is nevertheless necessary to base planning on certain assumptions and assumptions about a future we cannot know

[4336] It is not possible to get lost in the high degree of uncertainty in many fields

[4337] When making plans for the long-term development of the Armed Forces, it will therefore be necessary to identify both long-term continuity features, uncertain factors and possible unpredictable events that could entail dramatic disruptions in development

[4338] On this basis, planning must identify the requirements for the Armed Forces that will remain relatively fixed over a long period of time, and develop a defense structure with the robustness and flexibility to be able to handle challenges of a more uncertain and unpredictable nature

[4339] The military in a small country like Norway cannot afford or have the opportunity to uncritically jump on new trends that later turn out to be of a short-term nature

[4340] Although there is room to adjust the emphasis of various tasks, there will not be resources to change the entire structure and organization of the Armed Forces, even in a long-term perspective

[4341] Large and expensive structural elements, such as frigates, fighter aircraft and artillery, must be able to function as central elements in the force structure for many decades

[4342] The Armed Forces must therefore emphasize a range of fundamental capabilities that can handle the time-independent core tasks: defending Norway and Norwegian interests and values ​​against external threats and attacks

[4343] Experience shows that it is important to maintain the emphasis on such basic functions, even if current trends in a shorter period of time may seem to point in a different direction

[4344] In a period after the Cold War, for example, it might have seemed that the demand for military power would be primarily linked to stabilization operations in areas characterized by civil war and state collapse

[4345] A number of countries reorganized their defense forces to solely deal with these challenges

[4346] The Norwegian Armed Forces, for their part, were not only enabled to make relevant contributions to such operations, but also further developed their ability to handle sym-Prop

[4347] A defense for our time metric conflicts in our own immediate areas

[4348] It was a far-sighted strategy

[4349] The Government places great importance on the Armed Forces continuing to be a relevant instrument for defending Norwegian security and Norwegian interests, even if there is no concrete threat

[4350] In this way, the Armed Forces can fulfill their function as a war-preventing threshold and contribute to stability in our surrounding areas

[4351] Continuity features – relatively safe assumptions

[4352] There are few signs of changes in the strategic picture that will trigger sweeping new demands on the Defence Force in the foreseeable future

[4353] It can be assumed that the Armed Forces will continue to be able to carry out missions across the entire spectrum from peacetime tasks to crisis management nationally and internationally, as well as collective defense within an alliance framework

[4354] Although the pace of operations in international operations is expected to slow somewhat in the coming years, it can still be assumed that the Armed Forces will continue to make significant contributions to peace-support operations outside Norway, led by the UN, NATO and to some extent the EU

[4355] There are also no signs that international trends in the development of modern military power will change significantly

[4356] The emphasis of the last decade on developing more compact operational defense with high quality, advanced technology, high competence, responsiveness and mobility will likely continue

[4357] The defense will still need the ability to conduct high-intensity combat against a symmetrical adversary and, in addition, have the ability to respond appropriately and relevantly across the entire spectrum of conflicts

[4358] It can therefore be assumed that the Armed Forces will largely have the same main structure in the future

[4359] At the same time, it can be assumed that technological developments will reinforce some of today's trends

[4360] New opportunities will continue to open up to increase the effect of the force structure, not least through the use of advanced information and communication technology combined with changed organizational and management forms

[4361] It can also be assumed that technological developments will give rise to increasingly demanding security challenges

[4362] Threats in the digital space will continue to increase and become more complex, and this will create challenges for military operations, industry and critical infrastructure such as electricity supply and telecommunications

[4363] Developments within this and other technologies cannot be ignored, and the Armed Forces will have to continually find solutions to handle the challenges that arise

[4364] However, the Armed Forces have good conditions for integrating new technology into the existing force structure

[4365] Norway's platforms are flexible and can be upgraded with new technology when necessary

[4366] Internally in the defense sector, there will continue to be challenges related to the balance between operations and investments

[4367] This is a consequence of technological development and a more competence-intensive organization

[4368] The requirements for new and advanced expertise will be constantly evolving

[4369] This is described in more detail in Chapter

[4370] Relatively uncertain assumptions Within the framework of the main trends, there is still much that can vary over time

[4371] For example, even small changes in the security policy climate or in the need to ensure sound resource management can have an impact on the level of activity of the Armed Forces in Norway's surrounding areas

[4372] Contributions to international operations may also vary in size, duration and structure

[4373] The challenges that Norwegian forces face in such operations will vary greatly depending on the mission and the situation in the area of operation

[4374] The recent emphasis on anti-piracy operations shows that there may also be a need for other types of international efforts than those that dominate at a given time

[4375] It can be assumed that the operations will continue to be organized within the established multinational frameworks of the UN, NATO and to some extent the EU

[4376] Which operations will be relevant, however, will depend on the specific situation

[4377] Although Norway actively participates in the dialogue on the organization of international operations and promotes Norwegian views, Norwegian contributions will have to be adapted to the organizational framework agreed upon by the international community – including what capabilities are in demand

[4378] The development of infrastructure in Norway may also involve uncertain developments

[4379] There may be new and stricter environmental requirements, for example related to noise

[4380] Climate change and increased occurrence of extreme weather may raise new demands for robustness

[4381] Basic unpredictable events and changes

[4382] Single incidents and sweeping changes can have major consequences for the Armed Forces

[4383] Such events will always be difficult to predict

[4384] The examples below are for illustration purposes only

[4385] A defense for our time is based on events or developments that do not seem immediately likely today, but which could have great significance for the Armed Forces if they were to occur

[4386] A major symmetrical interstate conflict in another part of the world could have far-reaching consequences

[4387] Similarly, it would have major consequences if weapons of mass destruction were to be used in a conflict or in a terrorist attack in a way that makes the threat from such weapons over time even more prominent than it is today

[4388] Extensive political unrest, rebellions and civil war can also have serious ripple effects

[4389] Africa has long been characterized by such conflicts, and the wave of popular protests in North Africa and the Middle East has illustrated the potential for spread when such unrest breaks out in a region

[4390] It could be truly serious for the international situation if larger states with authoritarian governments were to be destabilized as a result of widespread internal uprisings

[4391] When it comes to Norway's immediate surroundings, there are currently few signs that point towards a dramatic deterioration of the threat situation

[4392] However, continued increased tension in the surrounding areas could have significant consequences for the prioritization of the Armed Forces' resources, for example related to the balance between efforts at home and abroad

[4393] Although the above examples do not appear likely today, they illustrate that the Defence must have the robustness and flexibility to be able to meet unexpected challenges and adapt to sudden changes

[4401] Cost development and long-term development

[4402] The Government emphasizes that the Armed Forces should be sized and organized to maintain a long-term and sound balance between operational structure and support structure

[4403] Development of the defence structure has a planning horizon that in most areas will have to go far beyond the established financial planning horizon

[4404] In a long-term perspective, there will also be considerable uncertainty related to both the global and national economies

[4405] From an international perspective, the defense sector is characterized by continuous development of new and increasingly advanced technology

[4406] The unit costs of some types of defense equipment tend to increase significantly from one generation to the next

[4407] The defense is therefore facing a continuing challenge related to cost growth in both operations and materiel investments

[4411] Some new systems can also take over the tasks of several older systems and thus make it possible to phase them out

[4412] Multinational collaboration is also receiving increasing attention as a strategy for addressing cost challenges

[4413] Cooperative arrangements such as Allied Ground Surveillance (AGS) and strategic airlift help introduce new capabilities in a way that shares the costs across multiple partners

[4414] Such cooperation is at the core of NATO's

[4415] Nordic defense cooperation within the framework of NORDEFCO also opens up such opportunities

[4416] Another strategy is to modernize and upgrade existing platforms so that their lifespan is extended while increasing operational capability

[4418] A defense of our time's relevance and applicability, even when they are in the final phase of their lifespan

[4420] Long-term capacity development must focus on military capabilities rather than renewing existing platforms

[4427] In larger operations, multinational organizations – the UN, NATO or the EU – will usually provide the framework for the effort

[4456] Establishment of missile defense under NATO auspices NATO must be able to prevent and meet the threats that member states are expected to face in the years ahead

[4457] The proliferation of weapons of mass destruction (chemical, biological and nuclear weapons) is one of the most serious threats to international security and stability

[4458] Several countries that are in the process of acquiring weapons of mass destruction have also made great strides in developing missile technology

[4459] We are faced with states and regimes that are not necessarily influenced by traditional deterrence

[4460] Europe is one of the areas particularly exposed to the threat from the proliferation of weapons of mass destruction and ballistic missiles

[4461] This is the background to NATO's initiative to develop defense against ballistic missiles

[4462] Missile defense is one element of a broad approach to reducing the significance of weapons of mass destruction, which also includes diplomacy and traditional non-proliferation work

[4463] NATO has long worked on developing missile defense, including through the Active Layered Theater Based Program

[4464] Missile Defense (ALTBMD

[4465] Together with our NATO allies, we decided at the Lisbon Summit in 2010 to develop a missile defense

[4466] Initially, this is done by expanding the scope of ALTBMD's command, control and communications systems beyond the protection of its own forces

[4467] The United States has offered its European Phased Adaptive Approach (EPAA) as a valuable national contribution

[4468] EPAA involves a phased development of missile defense in Europe

[4473] Missile defense is a concrete example of NATO's emphasis on "Smart Defense

[4475] It will address the need to protect Member States from one of the most serious threats we will face in the years ahead

[4579] Summary and implications – The Armed Forces and the future A sustainable defence structure requires targeted work to maintain a balance between resources, tasks, level of ambition and operational capability

[4580] Norway currently has a modern, well-balanced operational defense force, with the ability to carry out current tasks while at the same time investing in modern and future-oriented capabilities

[4581] The Government places great emphasis on ensuring that the defense sector continues to be developed based on a holistic and long-term perspective

[4582] In line with current security policy challenges, and in order to meet a changing world, the defense sector must be continuously renewed and improved

[4583] This is essential for the defense sector to continue to be a relevant security policy instrument for Norway

[4584] This implies an ongoing need to monitor changes in the environment as well as within the sector that may have significance in the longer term

[4585] Such analyses must be translated into a defense policy that guides the development of the Armed Forces and that can be specified in plans and measures to create the necessary restructuring and change

[4586] Foresight, flexibility and robustness are necessary to ensure a defense adapted to the needs of the times

[4587] The capabilities of the Armed Forces must be constantly renewed so that the Armed Forces remain a relevant instrument for safeguarding Norwegian security

[4717] Costs associated with new fighter jets

[4718] The purpose of this appendix is to account for key cost calculations related to the work of acquiring new combat aircraft, as well as the choice of a location solution for the combat aircraft

[4719] Furthermore, the methods, concepts and assumptions underlying the work are explained

[4720] First, the above-mentioned matters related to the acquisition of the fighter aircraft are explained

[4721] Next, an account is given of the corresponding aspects related to the cost calculations of localization solutions for new combat aircraft

[4722] Finally, definitions of the most important economic terms used are briefly listed

[4723] This appendix must be seen in light of chapters 6 and

[4724] Cost calculation – Acquisition of new fighter jets

[4725] Method and process for calculating acquisition and lifetime costs related to the acquisition of new combat aircraft The basis for the cost calculations related to acquisition and lifetime costs for new combat aircraft is a cost breakdown model (so called Work Breakdown Structure – WBS

[4726] This is a logical structuring of costs related to the acquisition and operation of the combat air force broken down into independent cost groups

[4727] Overall, this is divided into two

[4728] This part of the model includes cost elements that are expected to be incurred in the combat air force's investment phase (up to final delivery), including aircraft, weapons, basic investments in logistics and support organization

[4729] This part of the model includes cost elements expected to be incurred in the operational phase of the combat air force (until phasing out), including, among other things, upgrade costs, spare parts, fuel, education, training and maintenance

[4730] This also includes investments that are expected to be incurred during the operating period (30 years from the last aircraft delivered

[4731] Based on this cost structure, all relevant cost elements are sorted for the calculations to be made

[4732] The acquisition cost is calculated based on the costs included in the Investment Phase

[4733] The lifetime cost is calculated based on the costs included in both the investment phase and the operating phase

[4734] The costs included in the calculations are collected from a number of different sources

[4735] These include calculations from aircraft manufacturers and from other national authorities, own calculations and historical figures from previous comparable procurements

[4736] To ensure consistent assumptions and input values in the calculations, all cost data is adjusted to the same currency unit and point in time

[4737] For example, for the latest cost analysis for the fighter jet procurement (conducted in January 2012), June 2012 was chosen as the date

[4738] In the cost calculation, all costs are discounted to a present value at this point in time

[4739] Costs that will accrue in the future are spread out over time without discounting (real costs) and expected future real price growth is added before they are discounted to present value

[4740] Sections 2.2 and 2.3 below describe how the cost analyses are updated for price inflation and currency changes

[4741] The process of making the cost calculations takes place in several steps

[4742] First, the basic assumptions for the analysis are documented

[4743] The necessary data for the analysis is then collected and prepared

[4744] The third step is to assess uncertainty

[4745] Uncertainty is initially assessed based on estimate uncertainty and event uncertainty

[4746] The estimate uncertainty is assessed through so-called “three-point estimates” for each individual cost component

[4747] This means that a minimum value, an expected value and a maximum value are assessed for each cost component

[4748] These values ​​are set under a consistent set of assumptions

[4749] Furthermore, event uncertainty is assessed

[4750] These are elements of uncertainty that either occur or do not occur

[4751] The estimates are then assessed against the event uncertainties identified in the acquisition

[4752] Finally, the results are summarized in an uncertainty analysis

[4753] This analysis 2011–

[4755] These are normally stated as expected cost (P-50) and cost framework (with uncertainty allowance) (P

[4756] Update for price inflation in cost analyses

[4757] The fighter aircraft program, in line with most other high-tech projects, will be exposed to price developments in input factors that are higher than normal inflation measured by the consumer price index (CPI

[4758] It is therefore expected that this type of project will have so-called real price growth

[4759] The CPI is therefore not a sufficient basis for price-adjusting the cost picture

[4760] As there is no publicly available “fighter aircraft index” that can be used as a basis for price-adjusting the cost picture for fighter aircraft acquisition, a comparison index is used instead that is exposed to approximately the same growth factors that the F-35 program is expected to be exposed to during its lifetime

[4761] An already established index has been chosen here, which is prepared by an objective third party (in this case, Statistics Norway - SSB

[4762] In the subsequent analyses presented, the Statistics Norway index “Other Norwegian-produced consumer goods, affected by the world market due to high import content or raw material prices” is used as the basis for ongoing index adjustment of the program's cost development

[4763] The index is available in Statistics Norway's statistics bank on their website

[4764] Currency observations used in the cost analyses The cost analyses are based on an expected future dollar exchange rate (based on observations in the foreign exchange market) for each individual year in which payments are expected to take place

[4765] This is normal practice when dealing with future exchange rates as an uncertainty in large public procurements

[4766] These observations form the basis for both the pricing of the acquisition itself and the service life calculations

[4767] To ensure that the exchange rate assumptions are as objective as possible, the time for observation is determined well in advance of the observations being made

[4773] This expanded procurement solution formed the basis for the selection of the F-35 as the new combat aircraft, presented to the Storting in the autumn of 2008 in St.prp

[4839] Cost calculation – Localization of new fighter jets

[4840] Method and process for calculating acquisition and lifetime costs associated with siting alternatives for new combat aircraft

[4841] Following guidelines from the Ministry of Finance, a conceptual solution for a new fighter base structure has been prepared

[4842] This was published on November

[4843] The document contains a needs analysis, a strategy document that defines the objectives, a requirements document, an opportunities chapter, an alternatives analysis, and treatment of priced consequences in an uncertainty analysis

[4844] In the alternative analysis, 3 rounds of downsizing have been carried out

[4845] In the first shortlist, it is assessed which candidates meet the requirements to be suitable as sole proprietors

[4846] Only Bodø and Ørland are considered satisfactory candidates

[4847] Nevertheless, lifetime costs have been calculated for both Bodø, Ørland and Evenes as sole bases

[4848] In the second shortlist, it was assessed which candidates satisfy the requirements to be relevant QRA bases in combination with Ørland as the sole base in Southern Norway

[4849] Andøya, Evenes and Bodø were considered satisfactory candidates in the Conceptual Solution, and lifetime costs have therefore been calculated for these alternatives in combination with Ørland as the sole base

[4850] In the third downselection, it is considered which two-base combinations satisfy the requirements

[4851] The conclusion is that only Bodø together with Ørland, or Ørland together with Evenes are relevant combinations

[4852] Therefore, only lifetime costs have been calculated for these alternatives such as two bases

[4853] The lifetime costs are calculated over a time horizon of 40 years until 2052, when the F-35 is expected to be phased out

[4854] In order to compare the alternatives from a socio-economic perspective

[4855] Priced costs and revenues that affect actors other than the Armed Forces are identified and included

[4856] This has generally applied to civil aviation, but a number of non-priced consequences for the rest of society are also described in the conceptual solution

[4857] The conceptual solution has been subject to external quality assurance

[4858] The quality assurance officer approves the study, but had comments on the socio-economic analysis

[4859] sikker has carried out a separate and more comprehensive socio-economic analysis, which together with the Ministry of Defence's conceptual solution as a whole forms the basis for decisions related to the localization of the Armed Forces' new combat aircraft2. 3.2 Key figures and conclusions from the conceptual solution The calculated lifetime costs in the conceptual solution consist of investment and operating costs and are expressed as a present value

[4860] Present value calculations are suitable for comparing and ranking alternatives where investment and operating costs are phased in differently over time

[4861] The present value expresses the value of future cash flows, discounted at a discount rate of two percent

[4862] The calculations mainly include receipts and disbursements (cash flows) for personnel, equipment and infrastructure

[4863] The same unit cost growth has been used as in the fighter aircraft program, with a real growth of 2.0 percent per year for personnel and 1.6 percent per year for other cash flows

[4864] Uncertainty allowances are taken into account through separate uncertainty analyses of the input data, where expected values and dispersion measures are calculated for all types of cash flows

[4865] The calculations are supplemented with sensitivity analyses to reveal how robust the cost differences between the alternatives are to changes in, among other things, growth factors, discount rate and the length of the analysis period

[4903] Brief definition of economic terms

[4904] Here are listed and explained the most important economic terms used in the previous points

[4905] Present value is the value of a future amount or a future payment stream measured today

[4906] Another way of saying this is how much money one must set aside today to be able to pay all costs incurred during one's lifetime

[4907] This is done by adjusting the cash flow with a discount rate

[4908] The interest rate should reflect what you can expect to achieve in terms of return in the best alternative use for the state

[4909] Fixed crowns

[4910] Fixed kroner is when budgeted costs are stipulated at current prices without correction for general price increases

[4911] Fixed kroner must be stated with a base year that describes when the fixed point is

[4912] Nominal/current prices

[4913] Nominal kroner/current kroner

[4914] The amount something costs in a particular year without any form of inflation adjustment

[4915] Real kroner

[4916] Real kroner is a calculation of how large a planned future payment will be at the time of payment

[4917] Since compensation for ordinary price increases is provided annually in the Armed Forces' budgets, this is not included in the fighter aircraft program's calculation of real costs, so the real price increase is made up of the expected price increase above the ordinary price increase (inflation

[4918] The discount rate of 2% per year is provided by the Ministry of Finance (FIN

[4919] In the calculation, the costs are spread out over time and discounted to present value

[4920] This is in line with FIN recommendations and FIN's Guide to Socio-Economic Analysis

[4921] The risk associated with the estimates is addressed in assessments of cost ranges and influencing factors, addressed through the uncertainty analysis

[4922] Inflation is a persistent rise in prices or a fall in the purchasing power of money

[4923] Inflation can only be calculated historically

[4924] Expectations of inflation in the future can, for example, be calculated through the inflation target or models

[4925] Real price inflation is the price increase within a market or product group that goes beyond ordinary inflation

[4926] For example, the price increase in the housing market in recent years has been greater than ordinary inflation

[4927] The part of the real price increase due to inflation is excluded from the F-35 program's calculations, as this is compensated annually through the state budget

[4928] Uncertainty levels for cost estimates P-50 value

[4929] This is the cost framework within which the project is most likely to be implemented

[4930] Contains a minor uncertainty provision for expected additions

[4931] Normally referred to as “expected cost” P-85 value

[4932] P-85 is a cost framework with an uncertainty allowance and reflects a framework that with 85% probability will be able to stay within

[4933] The uncertainty provision comes as an addition to the expected cost framework (P-50) and is not normally available to the person responsible for implementation
